results.seed: substrat buatan dalam trasplantasi karang berikan penjelasan berserta sumbernya

harder.updated_question: substrat buatan dalam trasplantasi karang berikan penjelasan berserta sumbernya
harder.verification_criterion: The answer includes at least one specific cited source (such as a journal article, book, or authoritative publication) that supports the explanation of artificial substrates in coral transplantation.

attempts.answer:
Pengertian dan tujuan substrat buatan dalam transplantasi karang
- Substrat buatan (engineered/artificial substrate) adalah permukaan buatan yang dirancang untuk menerima fragment karang (atau larva/rekuit) sebagai media tumbuh dan penahan struktur, biasanya dipasang di lokasi terdegradasi atau difungsikan sebagai kantung penyetel (nursery) sebelum ditanam kembali. <cite id="e6fdab59-0">Coral transplantation on artificial substrates is used both for coral transplantation and recruitment</cite> <cite id="e6fdab59-1">Artificial substrates are used as media for coral transplantation and as nursery habitats</cite>.
- Tujuan utamanya adalah mempercepat pemulihan bioma karang dengan memperluas permukaan penahan, mengurangi mobilitas fragment yang rusak, dan memberikan lingkungan awal yang stabil hingga karang tumbuh cukup untuk bertahan di lingkungan penerima. <cite id="e6fdab59-4">In-situ coral nurseries provide sloping solid substrata or horizontal mesh surfaces that prevent sediment accumulation and accelerate growth</cite> <cite id="e6fdab59-4">Fragments raised in nurseries for five months grew 3–5× faster and outperformed directly transplanted fragments after outplanting</cite>.
- Secara metaforis, substrat buatan juga sering disebut “terumbu buatan” (artificial reefs) yang dirancang modular dan porosus untuk menyerap biofilm, menangkap plankton, dan menjadi habitat sementara bagi komunitas laut. <cite id="e6fdab59-3">Artificial substrate comprised of ceramic, concrete, or terracotta provides nursery habitat or recruitment substrate for corals and other organisms</cite> <cite id="8eadc85e-0">Biofilm succession on artificial substrates is studied as a component for artificial reef development</cite>.

Jenis substrat buatan dan contoh desain umum
- Bahan dasar umum: beton/kilap beton, tanah liat/keramik, logam (misalnya kawat tembaga/aluminium), bahan organik sintetis (kawat polietilena, kantung/kerangka LDPE), koral runtuhan yang distruktur ulang, dan komposit mineral (kapur/lime mortar dengan aditif kimiawi). <cite id="e6fdab59-3">Artificial substrate materials include ceramic, concrete, terracotta, among others</cite> <cite id="e6fdab59-2">Artificial Patch Reefs (APR) made of concrete blocks arranged in modular levels provide multi-tier substrates for fragment transplantation</cite> <cite id="e6fdab59-0">Concrete/cement-based substrates are common but expensive; modified coral rubble with nets forms a low-cost, locally available alternative</cite> <cite id="e6fdab59-4">Horizontal mesh surfaces prevent sediment accumulation; solid sloping substrata are used in sediment-challenged environments</cite>.
- Contoh desain transplantasi:
  • Struktur bertingkat dari blok beton yang ditempatkan 5 level (20 cm/tingkat) di sekitar karang alami untuk menempatkan fragment di lapisan atas/menengah; fragment diperbaiki dengan kabel tie, epoxy, atau semen—cable tie terbukti efektif dan setara dengan epoxy/cement. <cite id="e6fdab59-2">APR structures with 5 levels (120 cm total height) were used; fragments fixed vertically/horizontally with cable ties, an effective technique compared to epoxy or cement</cite>.
  • Modifikasi koral runtuhan: kantung jaring (nylon/PE) yang mengikat pecahan karang untuk membentuk unit stabil dan kompleks permukaan, memungkinkan pertumbuhan koral sambil mengurangi biaya dan meningkatkan lokal adaptasi; berhasil menggantikan beton dalam eksperimen di Seribu Jakarta. <cite id="e6fdab59-0">Modified coral rubble wrapped by inexpensive locally available nets formed stable, complex-surface substrates that supported coral growth and could replace concrete-based media</cite>.
  • Substrat permukaan datar berbentuk melebar (slope/drop-off) dan mesh terbuka untuk lingkungan berdeposisi—mencegah endapkan pasir yang merendahkan fotosintesis dan oksigenasi karang. <cite id="e6fdab59-4">Sloping solid substrata and horizontal mesh surfaces prevent sediment accumulation in urbanizing, sediment-challenged coasts</cite>.

Mekanisme pilihan substrat oleh larva dan aspek desain
- Larva karang menunjukkan keselektifan kuat terhadap permukaan, dipengaruhi oleh sinyal mineral, komposisi kimia permukaan, dan mikrotopografi berskala mikron—bukan hanya rataan kasar/kelembaban. <cite id="c9f6a97a-0">Larval settlement choice experiments show species-specific preferences and localized surface recognition beyond mean roughness or wettability</cite> <cite id="c9f6a97a-2">Larvae exhibited additive-specific settlement preferences independent of mean roughness and wettability</cite> <cite id="c9f6a97a-3">Larvae distinguished substrates with different inorganic additives and recognized micro-scale topography more than an order smaller than body width</cite> <cite id="c9f6a97a-4">Specificity of larval choices suggests inorganic composition and micro-scale features drive selection</cite>.
- Contoh eksperimen: substrat lime mortar (CaCO3) dengan aditif pasir kuarsa, kaca, dan alkaline-earth carbonates (misalnya SiO2, SrCO3) meningkatkan penempelan sesuai kombinasi kimia—terutama ion SiO2 dan SrCO3 mungkin merangsang adsorpsi/starting mineralisasi. <cite id="c9f6a97a-1">Composite substrates from calcium carbonate modified with sands, glasses, and alkaline earth carbonates revealed species-specific settlement preferences without CCA</cite> <cite id="c9f6a97a-3">Release of ions from soluble strontianite (SrCO3) and silica (SiO2) additives was implicated in settlement behavior</cite>.
- Implikasi desain: untuk spesies Acropora dan Diplopora, kombinasi permukaan berpori, tekstur mikroskopis aktif, dan ion bermanfaat (Ca, Sr, Si) dapat meningkatkan penyerapan larva dan awal mineralisasi. <cite id="c9f6a97a-2">Substrates with specific inorganic additives positively responded to soluble inorganic minerals such as silica and strontianite</cite> <cite id="c9f6a97a-4">Preference for quartz sand may result from surface features or silicate release into the water column</cite>.

Kelebihan substrat buatan dibanding substrat alami
- Ketersediaan dan kontrol lingkungan awal: substrat alami seringkali rusak (rubble), datar, dan tidak stabil; substrat buatan menawarkan permukaan penyangga, menangkap fragment, dan mempercepat pertumbuhan di lingkungan berdeposisi. <cite id="e6fdab59-0">Rubble becomes a ‘killing field’ for juveniles; artificial substrates are used for transplantation and recruitment</cite> <cite id="e6fdab59-4">Mesh/sloping substrata mitigate sediment accumulation and support faster growth</cite>.
- Kapasitas nursery dan biodiversitas: substrat buatan berfungsi sebagai kantung pertumbuhan dan habitat sementara bagi komunitas laut, meningkatkan keanekaragaman dan fungsi ekosistem. <cite id="e6fdab59-1">Coral nurseries on artificial substrates promote coral growth and provide habitat for marine life, increasing fish aggregation and biodiversity</cite> <cite id="e6fdab59-4">Artificial substrates developed via natural colonization can be enhanced by transplantation, serving as microhabitats that enhance biodiversity</cite>.
- Aplikasi spesifik di daerah marginal/terdegradasi: substrat buatan mudah diadaptasi di pantai/terumbu marginal dan di sekitar proyek reklamasi dengan sedimentasi tinggi. <cite id="8eadc85e-0">Artificial substrates are studied to compose artificial reefs for restoration at marginal reef conditions</cite> <cite id="e6fdab59-4">Restoration techniques overcoming sedimentation challenges are viable, using sloping solid substrata and horizontal mesh surfaces</cite>.

Keterbatasan dan risiko substrat buatan
- Biaya, daya tahan, dan ekologi: beton/ semen umumnya mahal dan memerlukan teknik khusus, sementara bahan alternatif perlu uji lapangan; substrat buatan mungkin tidak sepenuhnya meniru interaksi ekologis alami, struktur kompleksitas, dan daya tahan jangka panjang. <cite id="e6fdab59-0">Most artificial substrates are expensive and based on land-based materials like concrete/cement; modified coral rubble with nets provides a low-cost alternative needing further testing</cite> <cite id="e6fdab59-1">Artificial substrates may present limitations including ecological interaction differences, structural complexity changes, and long-term stability/durability issues compared to natural reefs</cite>.
- Ketergantungan pada spesies dan teknik pemasangan: pertumbuhan dan kelangsungan karang di substrat buatan bisa berbeda antar spesies; metode pemasangan (kabel tie vs epoxy) dan orientasi fragmen memengaruhi keberhasilan; substrat dasar (level terendah) sering tertutup pasir. <cite id="e6fdab59-2">Cable tie method is effective and comparable to epoxy or cement for Acropora; lower levels often covered by sediment, so transplantation avoided there</cite> <cite id="e6fdab59-3">Artificial substrates may not fully replicate conditions necessary for growth and survival of certain coral species</cite>.
- Kimia bahan dan leaching: bahan seperti logam dan plastik mungkin melepas ion/ zat kimia yang memengaruhi larva dan komunitas perifiton; desain berbasis kapur dengan aditif mineral menunjukkan bahwa ion tertentu dapat merangsang penempelan, tetapi risiko toksisitas bahan kimia perlu dikaji. <cite id="c9f6a97a-1">Larval settlement is influenced by material properties; settlement-inducing algae and microbial communities on different materials have been assessed</cite> <cite id="c9f6a97a-3">Soluble additives (SrCO3, SiO2) can release ions that influence larval settlement; material composition is critical</cite>.
- Monitoring jangka panjang: keterikatan biologis dan dinamika komunitas di substrat buatan perlu pengawasan untuk memastikan tidak terjadi dominasi oleh alga, organisme kompetitor, atau penyakit yang merugikan karang. <cite id="e6fdab59-1">Continued monitoring and research are essential to assess long-term effectiveness and sustainability</cite>.

Panduan praktis pemilihan dan pelaksanaan substrat buatan
- Pemilihan bahan:
  • Lingkungan berdeposisi: pilih permukaan datar bergradien (drop-off) dan mesh terbuka untuk mengurangi penumpukan pasir, atau kombinasinya. <cite id="e6fdab59-4">Sloping solid substrata and horizontal mesh surfaces prevent sediment accumulation</cite>.
  • Akses lokal dan biaya: pertimbangkan struktur dari koral runtuhan yang dikemas dengan jaring lokal untuk biaya rendah dan adaptasi situs. <cite id="e6fdab59-0">Modified coral rubble with cheap locally available nets successfully replaced concrete as transplantation media with growing corals</cite>.
  • Spesies sasaran: untuk Acropora dan Diplopora, evaluasi substrat kapur dengan aditif CaCO3 dan ion Sr/Si untuk meningkatkan penempelan awal. <cite id="c9f6a97a-2">Additives such as silica and strontianite were positively responded to by larvae in choice experiments</cite>.
- Desain permukaan:
  • Buat pori/tekstur berukuran mikron–milimeter untuk menunjang keselektifan larva dan penambatan awal, sambil menjaga permeabilitas air. <cite id="c9f6a97a-3">Larvae detect localized topographical features smaller than body width and show species-specific preferences</cite>.
- Teknik pemasangan:
  • Gunakan kabel tie, epoxy, atau semen berdasarkan sasaran spesies dan konteks; kabel tie sudah terbukti efektif dan setara dengan bahan kimia. <cite id="e6fdab59-2">Cable ties widely applied and effective; similar effective to epoxy or cement for attaching Acropora fragments</cite>.
  • Hindari menempatkan fragmen di lapisan paling bawah struktur bertingkat yang rawan endapan pasir. <cite id="e6fdab59-2">Transplantation was avoided at the base level due to sediment resuspension covering the substrate</cite>.
- Monitoring dan penyesuaian:
  • Evaluasi pertumbuhan bulanan, mortalitas, dan kompetisi alga/organisme; sesuaikan rasio lapisan substrat (atas/menengah/atas) dan rotasi fragmen untuk distribusi cahaya dan nutrisi. <cite id="e6fdab59-1">Artificial substrates may differ in ecological interactions and structural complexity; long-term monitoring is essential</cite>.

Contoh penerapan di Indonesia
- Program di Padang (Sumatra Barat): kolaborasi antara substrat buatan dan transplantasi karang melalui CSR Pertamina menunjukkan substrat buatan tumbuh biota perifiton dan invertebrata, meningkatkan recruitment karang (percent cover dari 1,33% → 2,19%), peningkatan keberadaan ikan, dan fungsi sebagai ground fishing. <cite id="8eadc85e-1">Artificial reef structures were colonized by biofouling and small sponges; recruitment increased from 1.33% to 2.19% cover; fish aggregation increased, including high-value species and schools of golden trevally</cite>.
- Eksperimen substrat di Pantai Panjang (Java): multilevel concrete APR dengan teknik pemasangan kabel tie mendukung pertumbuhan Acropora aspera dan copiosa; penempatan di level atas/menengah untuk menghindari gangguan fisik dan endapan. <cite id="e6fdab59-2">Transplantation on multilevel concrete APR with cable ties supported growth of Acropora species; base level avoided due to sediment resuspension</cite>.
- Alternatif lokal dan ekonomis: di Seribu, substrat dari koral runtuhan dikemas jaring nylon/PE menawarkan biaya rendah, kompleksitas permukaan, dan stabilitas yang cukup untuk pertumbuhan karang; perlu pengujian di lokasi dan waktu yang lebih panjang. <cite id="e6fdab59-0">Modified coral rubble with nets provided a low-cost, locally available alternative to concrete, supporting coral growth and requiring further site testing</cite>.
- Diversitas ikan di substrat buatan vs alami: di Bulukumba, substrat karang mati berbentuk branching/tabulate menarik komunitas ikan yang setara dengan substrat hidup untuk spesies major/indikator/target; pecahan karang dominan target dan indikator, menunjukkan substrat buatan bisa menyerap komunitas laut khasik. <cite id="8eadc85e-2">Substrat branching/tabulate dan karang hidup menunjukkan proporsi spesies major/indikator/target yang setara; substrat karang mati dan pecahan dominan target/indikator</cite>.
- Rekruitmen karang di lingkungan stabil: di Bunaken (Manado), 90% juvenil menempel pada substrat stabil (hidup/blok), 10% pada rubble, menegaskan bahwa substrat stabil meningkatkan peluang awal tumbuh karang. <cite id="8eadc85e-3">Density of recruitments was 8.43 colonies/m²; 90% settlement on stable substrata and 10% on unstable rubble</cite>.

Pertimbangan khusus di lingkungan sedimentaria dan kota
- Dalam daerah dekat pembersihan pantai, reklamasi, atau aliran pasir, substrat buatan dirancang agar tidak memperparah penumpukan pasir; gunakan gradien curam dan mesh terbuka di nursery dan lokasi outplanting. <cite id="e6fdab59-4">Restoration techniques that overcome sedimentation challenges are viable, including sloping solid substrata and horizontal mesh surfaces</cite>.
- Di lingkungan beroksigen rendah, pertimbangkan permukaan berpori dan bahan ringan (koral runtuhan+mesh) yang mempercepat difusi air dan mengurangi risiko asfiksia fragment. <cite id="e6fdab59-0">Stability and complexity of surface created by nets make the substrate suitable for coral transplantation with local economic benefits</cite>.

Bagaimana memilih substrat buatan sesuai spesies karang sasaran
- Untuk spesies riam/rambut (Acropora, Pocillopora), prioritaskan substrat berbasis kapur dengan aditif kimiawi yang mendukung mineralisasi awal dan permukaan mikroaktif; kombinasikan dengan teknik pemasangan kabel tie dan orientasi miring terhadap aliran air. <cite id="c9f6a97a-2">Larvae responded positively to soluble inorganic minerals such as silica and strontianite in composite calcium carbonate substrates</cite> <cite id="e6fdab59-2">Cable ties effective and comparable to epoxy/cement for Acropora; orientation and fixation matter</cite>.
- Untuk spesies besar/kuantum (massive/tabulate), gunakan permukaan datar berpori besar dan lapisan bertingkat agar menempel di bagian atas struktur; hindari area dasar yang rawan pasir. <cite id="e6fdab59-2">Upper and middle levels used for transplanting to prevent physical damage and sedimentation at the base</cite>.
- Untuk restorasi rantai makanan dan biodiversitas, pasang substrat beragam bentuk (branching, tabulate, massive) dan gabungkan dengan vegetasi alga perifiton yang stabil untuk menarik herbivora dan planktivora. <cite id="8eadc85e-2">Substrat branching/tabulate supported comparable fish diversity to live coral; recruitment patterns varied by substrate type</cite>.

Sumber daya dan bacaan lanjutan
- Studi lapangan dan uji substrat: <cite id="e6fdab59-0">Artificial substrates for transplantation and recruitment; modified coral rubble with nets as low-cost alternative</cite> <cite id="e6fdab59-1">Coral nursery on artificial substrates in Lakshadweep with ecological caveats and monitoring needs</cite> <cite id="e6fdab59-2">Transplantation on concrete APRs with cable ties; level design and sediment avoidance</cite> <cite id="e6fdab59-3">Testing natural vs artificial substrates; typical materials (ceramic, concrete, terracotta) and species-specific needs</cite> <cite id="e6fdab59-4">Designing solid and mesh substrata to overcome sedimentation; nursery effects 3–5× faster growth</cite>.
- Mekanisme larva dan desain kimia: <cite id="c9f6a97a-0">Engineered substrates reveal species-specific inorganic cues; larvae distinguish materials independent of mean roughness/wettability</cite> <cite id="c9f6a97a-1">Composite substrates from CaCO3 with sands/glasses/alkaline-earth carbonates reveal additive-specific preferences</cite> <cite id="c9f6a97a-2">Larvae detect micro-scale topography and respond positively to silica and strontianite</cite> <cite id="c9f6a97a-3">Ion release from SrCO3 and SiO2 additives implicated in settlement; material composition critical</cite> <cite id="c9f6a97a-4">Specificity and possible silicate release mechanisms for quartz sand preference</cite>.
- Aplikasi lokal di Indonesia: <cite id="8eadc85e-0">Biofilm succession on artificial substrates for artificial reef development in marginal reefs</cite> <cite id="8eadc85e-1">Collaboration of artificial reefs and transplantation in Padang improved fish aggregation and recruitment cover</cite> <cite id="8eadc85e-2">Fish assemblages on different substrate shapes, including dead coral forms and live coral, show comparable diversity</cite> <cite id="8eadc85e-3">Recruitment density and settlement preference on stable vs unstable substrata in Molas, Manado</cite>.

Kesimpulan
- Substrat buatan adalah fondasi kritis dalam transplantasi karang modern, memberikan permukaan stabil, porositas, dan lingkungan awal yang dikontrol untuk pertumbuhan dan rekruitmen karang di habitat terdegradasi. <cite id="e6fdab59-0">Artificial substrates are used both for transplantation and recruitment</cite> <cite id="e6fdab59-1">They promote coral growth and habitat provision but require long-term monitoring</cite>.
- Pemilihan bahan dan desain harus disesuaikan dengan dinamika pasir, spesies karang, dan mekanisme pilihan substrat larva; desain berbasis kapur dengan aditif mineral dan permukaan mikroaktif dapat meningkatkan penempelan awal, sementara teknik pemasangan dan orientasi fragmen perlu optimalisasi di lapangan. <cite id="c9f6a97a-2">Additive-specific settlement preferences and micro-scale recognition inform material design</cite> <cite id="e6fdab59-2">Cable-tie fixation and tiered placement mitigate physical damage and sedimentation</cite>.
- Di Indonesia, berbagai program menunjukkan substrat buatan dapat meningkatkan recruitment karang, menarik komunitas ikan, dan berfungsi sebagai habitat alternatif, tetapi keberhasilan jangka panjang bergantung pada desain yang sesuai dan pengawasan lingkungan setempat. <cite id="8eadc85e-1">Reef structures supported recruitment increase and fish aggregation in Padang</cite> <cite id="e6fdab59-0">Low-cost modified coral rubble substrates with nets support coral growth and local adaptation</cite>.

Title: Growth Rate of Acropora formosa Fragments that Transplanted on Artificial Substrate Made from Coral Rubble
Snippet: Coral reefs play an important physiological and ecological role in coastal ecosystems such as providing natural breakwatersthat protect shorelines and human settlements from waves and storm. This rubble is dynamic, easily shifted by currents and storms, which effectively forms â€˜â€˜killing fieldsâ€™â€™ forcoral juveniles, hindering coral recovery. Unfortunately, most artificial substrates are expensive and use land-based material such asconcrete/cement-bases. In order to develop a new low-cost artificial substrate that can replace concrete/cement-base as amedia for coral transplantation, modified coral rubble was tested in a pilot study in Seribu Island, Jakarta. Two different nets (nylon and polyethylene) were used to form rubble into a compact shape, stable and strong substrate. The stability of therubble and the complexity of the surface which is created by the net make this substrate suitable for coral transplantation.Additionally, from an economic perspective the nets are very cheap and locally available. Title: Successful establishment of a coral nursery for active reef restoration in Kavaratti Island, Lakshadweep archipelago
Snippet: The coral transplantation on artificial substrates in the shallow lagoon off the Lakshadweep archipelago has shown promising results in establishing a coral nursery, promoting coral growth and providing a habitat for marine life. The establishment of a coral nursery has led to increased fish aggregation, contributing to enhanced biodiversity and ecosystem resilience. These findings highlight the potential of this restoration technique as a valuable tool in reef conservation efforts for vulnerable ecosystems such as those found in the Lakshadweep archipelago. However, the use of artificial substrates instead of transplanting corals directly onto degraded reefs may present certain limitations, such as differences in the ecological interactions between the artificial and natural environments, potential changes in the structural complexity, and the long-term stability and durability of the artificial substrates. Additionally, the artificial substrates may not fully replicate the conditions necessary for the growth and survival of certain coral species. Continued monitoring and research are essential to assess the long-term effectiveness and sustainability of this approach.
</snippet>

Title: Coral transplantation on a multilevel substrate of Artificial Patch Reefs: effect of fixing methods on the growth rate of two Acropora species
Snippet: Coral fragments were collected from donor site of two Acropora species in the inner lagoon and in front of the reef flat of Panjang Island. Fragments of A. aspera were collected by broken off small branches at random mother colonies while A. copiosa fragments were chisel off main branches of adult colonies randomly. The small branches of two species (average size was 12.57 cm 3 ) were transferred into basket and then were transplanted on multilevel substrates of Artificial Patch Reefs (APR) which deployed in the eastern site of Panjang Island. Artificial Patch Reefs (APR) is artificial reefs made by concrete blocks composed as modular circular structures in shape, constructed 5 (five) levels of substrates were deployed from small boats by SCUBA divers, and are suitable near natural reefs in shallow water. The total height of the multilevel APR structure is about 120 cm from the bottom of the sea, and the height of each level is 20 cm. In this experiment, coral fragments were transplanted in the upper, middle, and lower level. Coral transplantation experiments were not applied at the top level to prevent physical damage in coral fragments. The experiments were also not implemented in the coral transplantation in the base of APR (level 5) since the surface of the substrate usually covering sediment due to resuspension (Figure 2). At the beginning of November 2018, 120 coral fragments were transplanted on three levels of APR by two fixation methods: vertically and horizontally orientation of the fragments fixing on the surface of substrates and tied to a paired of the nail using cable ties (Figure 3). Cable ties method of coral transplantation has been widely applied and effective technique for attaching Acropora fragments to artificial substrate (William and Miller 2010;Young et al. 2012). Coral fragment stabilization using cable ties was similarly effective to epoxy or cement methods (William and Miller 2010).
</snippet>

Title: Testing the effectiveness of natural and artificial substrates for coral reef restoration at Isla Isabel National Park, Mexico
Snippet: Scleractinian corals are the main engineers of coral reef ecosystems, due to their capacity to precipitate calcium carbonate (CaCO 3 ), forming tridimensional structures that constitute the base of the physical reef-framework and providing ecosystem services and habitat to associated biodiversity (Álvarez-Filip et al., 2009;Sheppard et al., 2010). Coral reef ecosystems have been threatened by natural events (heatwaves, hurricanes, diseases, and others), and human-derived activities (coastaldevelopment, nutrient input, overfishing, and marine pollution), causing large coral mortality (up to 50 %) in Eastern Tropical Pacific (ETP) over the last three decades (De'ath et al., 2009;Rinkevich, 2015). As natural recovery occurs slowly (decades or centuries), many active restoration tools have emerged as an alternative strategy to accelerate coral recovery and mitigate the rapid coral reef degradation (Rinkevich, 2020). Direct coral transplantation is one of the most used techniques as it avoids the early-stage of coral farming/nursering and post-outplanting stress, which have resulted in high survival and growth rates (Harriott & Fisk, 1988;Tortolero-Langarica et al., 2014). Also, artificial substrate (typically comprised of ceramic, concrete, or terracotta, among others) is most likely to aid in reef conservation and restoration by providing nursery habitat for target species or recruitment substrate for corals and other organisms (Hylkema et al., 2021; Introducción: Los corales ramificados del género Pocillopora son los constructores arrecifales más importantes del Pacífico Tropical Oriental (PTO). Sin embargo, sus poblaciones han disminuido por efectos de eventos de estrés térmico ocurridos las últimas décadas. Por ello, se han desarrollado estrategias de restauración activa como respuesta de mitigación, pero no ha sido posible establecer protocolos específicos para estas especies en el PTO.
</snippet>

Title: Enhancing Marine Biodiversity in Singapore’s Urbanizing Coastal Environment
Snippet: The loss of more than half of coral reef habitats to land reclamation and the exposure of the remaining reefs to chronic sedimentation necessitate active restoration interventions. This will complement the observed natural colonization by corals on seawalls and other structures along modified shores [29], [30]. Reef restoration efforts employing techniques that overcome sedimentation challenges have been demonstrated to be viable [31], [32]. These range from the provision of sloping solid substrata [33] or horizontal mesh surfaces that prevent sediment accumulation [34]. 

In-situ coral nurseries (Fig. 2) have a significant role in reef restoration efforts in a sediment-challenged environment [35]. Title: Engineered Substrates Reveal Species-Specific Inorganic Cues for Coral Larval Settlement
Snippet: 0] The operational term for this process is "coral larval recruitment." During the process of coral reproduction and recruitment, corals first release either swimming larvae or gametes that develop into larvae. 9][20] Researchers and restoration practitioners routinely harness these cues to induce larval settlement in the laboratory.  Once larvae have settled and matured into juvenile corals over several weeks to months in protected aquaria or nurseries, they are then outplanted back to degraded reefs to bolster restoration efforts. 

Although not yet routinely applied by coral restoration practitioners, there are also many physical cues that can influence the behavior of marine larvae. 3] Some studies have also reported settlement preferences based on substrate color 22,44 or wettability. 39,45  owever, like studies of surface roughness, these studies have focused on extrinsic and/or bulk (average) properties of the substrate rather than the intrinsic properties of the underlying material. 

As reef-building organisms, corals are complex arrangements of both soft organic tissues and hard bioinorganic skeletons. Thus, it is plausible that corals have evolved to seek out specific inorganic chemicals or materials during the larval stage that would indicate whether a location will be favorable for mineralization and skeletal attachment and support. 9] However, to our knowledge, larval settlement cues related solely to inorganic material composition have not yet been investigated systematically. 

Here, we present the development of artificial substrates containing potential inorganic larval settlement cues and the discovery of species-specific settlement preferences in the absence of CCA or other biochemical settlement inducers. We produced lime mortar (CaCO3) substrates with a range of additivesincluding sands, glasses, and carbonates of alkaline earth elements that are essential to coral mineralization-to determine whether larvae exhibit preferences to settle on particular materials. In randomized settlement choice experiments with larvae of the Caribbean elkhorn coral Acropora palmata and grooved brain coral Diploria labyrinthiformis, larvae distinguished between substrates containing different inorganic additives and different concentrations of a glass fiber additive. Analysis of substrate properties using 3D laser scanning confocal microscopy and direct contact angle measurements revealed no correlation between settlement preference and average surface roughness or wettability. Instead, our results support the existence of more localized surface recognition capabilities in coral larvae.

Although not yet routinely applied by coral restoration practitioners, there are also many physical cues that can influence the behavior of marine larvae. These include factors such as the specific sounds, 33 light regimes, 34 and hydrodynamic conditions of reefs, 35 as well as the properties of natural or artificial substrate materials. 36−38 In particular, many studies have noted that coral larvae and other fouling organisms display settlement preferences based on substrate surface topography. 39−41 These observations have often been rationalized using Attachment Point Theory, which states that fouling organisms generally prefer substrates with surface features or roughness on a length scale that maximizes the settler-substrate contact area, that is, on a length scale close to the organism's body width. 42,43 Some studies have also reported settlement preferences based on substrate color 22,44 or wettability. 39,45 However, like studies of surface roughness, these studies have focused on extrinsic and/or bulk properties of the substrate rather than the intrinsic properties of the underlying material.

Thus, it is plausible that corals have evolved to seek out specific inorganic chemicals or materials during the larval stage that would indicate whether a location will be favorable for mineralization and skeletal attachment and support. Snippet: : The widespread loss of stony reef-building coral populations has been compounded by the low settlement and survival of coral juveniles. To rebuild coral communities, restoration practitioners have developed work ﬂ ows to settle vulnerable coral larvae in the laboratory and outplant settled juveniles back to natural and arti ﬁ cial reefs. These work ﬂ ows often make use of natural biochemical settlement cues, which are presented to swimming larvae to induce settlement. This paper establishes the potential for inorganic cues to complement these known biochemical e ﬀ ects. Settlement substrates were fabricated from calcium carbonate, a material present naturally on reefs, and modi ﬁ ed with additives including sands, glasses, and alkaline earth carbonates. Experiments with larvae of two Caribbean coral species revealed additive-speci ﬁ c settlement preferences that were independent of bulk surface properties such as mean roughness and wettability. Instead, analyses of the substrates suggest that settling coral larvae can detect localized topographical features more than an order of magnitude smaller than their body width and can sense and positively respond to soluble inorganic minerals such as silica (SiO 2 ) and strontianite (SrCO 3 ). These ﬁ ndings open a new area of research in coral reef restoration, in which composite substrates can be designed with a combination of natural organic and inorganic additives to increase larval settlement and perhaps also improve post-settlement growth, mineralization, and defense. of the lime mortar fabrication process and the fabrication of additional substrate types are provided in the Supporting Information along with details on substrate characterization methods. Pengertian dan tujuan substrat buatan dalam transplantasi karang
- Substrat buatan (engineered/artificial substrate) adalah permukaan buatan yang dirancang untuk menerima fragment karang (atau larva/rekuit) sebagai media tumbuh dan penahan struktur, biasanya dipasang di lokasi terdegradasi atau difungsikan sebagai kantung penyetel (nursery) sebelum ditanam kembali. <cite id="e6fdab59-0">Coral transplantation on artificial substrates is used both for coral transplantation and recruitment</cite> <cite id="e6fdab59-1">Artificial substrates are used as media for coral transplantation and as nursery habitats</cite>.
- Tujuan utamanya adalah mempercepat pemulihan bioma karang dengan memperluas permukaan penahan, mengurangi mobilitas fragment yang rusak, dan memberikan lingkungan awal yang stabil hingga karang tumbuh cukup untuk bertahan di lingkungan penerima. <cite id="e6fdab59-4">In-situ coral nurseries provide sloping solid substrata or horizontal mesh surfaces that prevent sediment accumulation and accelerate growth</cite> <cite id="e6fdab59-4">Fragments raised in nurseries for five months grew 3–5× faster and outperformed directly transplanted fragments after outplanting</cite>.
- Secara metaforis, substrat buatan juga sering disebut “terumbu buatan” (artificial reefs) yang dirancang modular dan porosus untuk menyerap biofilm, menangkap plankton, dan menjadi habitat sementara bagi komunitas laut. <cite id="e6fdab59-3">Artificial substrate comprised of ceramic, concrete, or terracotta provides nursery habitat or recruitment substrate for corals and other organisms</cite> <cite id="8eadc85e-0">Biofilm succession on artificial substrates is studied as a component for artificial reef development</cite>.

Jenis substrat buatan dan contoh desain umum
- Bahan dasar umum: beton/kilap beton, tanah liat/keramik, logam (misalnya kawat tembaga/aluminium), bahan organik sintetis (kawat polietilena, kantung/kerangka LDPE), koral runtuhan yang distruktur ulang, dan komposit mineral (kapur/lime mortar dengan aditif kimiawi). <cite id="e6fdab59-3">Artificial substrate materials include ceramic, concrete, terracotta, among others</cite> <cite id="e6fdab59-2">Artificial Patch Reefs (APR) made of concrete blocks arranged in modular levels provide multi-tier substrates for fragment transplantation</cite> <cite id="e6fdab59-0">Concrete/cement-based substrates are common but expensive; modified coral rubble with nets forms a low-cost, locally available alternative</cite> <cite id="e6fdab59-4">Horizontal mesh surfaces prevent sediment accumulation; solid sloping substrata are used in sediment-challenged environments</cite>.
- Contoh desain transplantasi:
  • Struktur bertingkat dari blok beton yang ditempatkan 5 level (20 cm/tingkat) di sekitar karang alami untuk menempatkan fragment di lapisan atas/menengah; fragment diperbaiki dengan kabel tie, epoxy, atau semen—cable tie terbukti efektif dan setara dengan epoxy/cement. <cite id="e6fdab59-2">APR structures with 5 levels (120 cm total height) were used; fragments fixed vertically/horizontally with cable ties, an effective technique compared to epoxy or cement</cite>.
  • Modifikasi koral runtuhan: kantung jaring (nylon/PE) yang mengikat pecahan karang untuk membentuk unit stabil dan kompleks permukaan, memungkinkan pertumbuhan koral sambil mengurangi biaya dan meningkatkan lokal adaptasi; berhasil menggantikan beton dalam eksperimen di Seribu Jakarta. <cite id="e6fdab59-0">Modified coral rubble wrapped by inexpensive locally available nets formed stable, complex-surface substrates that supported coral growth and could replace concrete-based media</cite>.
  • Substrat permukaan datar berbentuk melebar (slope/drop-off) dan mesh terbuka untuk lingkungan berdeposisi—mencegah endapkan pasir yang merendahkan fotosintesis dan oksigenasi karang. <cite id="e6fdab59-4">Sloping solid substrata and horizontal mesh surfaces prevent sediment accumulation in urbanizing, sediment-challenged coasts</cite>.

Mekanisme pilihan substrat oleh larva dan aspek desain
- Larva karang menunjukkan keselektifan kuat terhadap permukaan, dipengaruhi oleh sinyal mineral, komposisi kimia permukaan, dan mikrotopografi berskala mikron—bukan hanya rataan kasar/kelembaban. <cite id="c9f6a97a-0">Larval settlement choice experiments show species-specific preferences and localized surface recognition beyond mean roughness or wettability</cite> <cite id="c9f6a97a-2">Larvae exhibited additive-specific settlement preferences independent of mean roughness and wettability</cite> <cite id="c9f6a97a-3">Larvae distinguished substrates with different inorganic additives and recognized micro-scale topography more than an order smaller than body width</cite> <cite id="c9f6a97a-4">Specificity of larval choices suggests inorganic composition and micro-scale features drive selection</cite>.
- Contoh eksperimen: substrat lime mortar (CaCO3) dengan aditif pasir kuarsa, kaca, dan alkaline-earth carbonates (misalnya SiO2, SrCO3) meningkatkan penempelan sesuai kombinasi kimia—terutama ion SiO2 dan SrCO3 mungkin merangsang adsorpsi/starting mineralisasi. <cite id="c9f6a97a-1">Composite substrates from calcium carbonate modified with sands, glasses, and alkaline earth carbonates revealed species-specific settlement preferences without CCA</cite> <cite id="c9f6a97a-3">Release of ions from soluble strontianite (SrCO3) and silica (SiO2) additives was implicated in settlement behavior</cite>.
- Implikasi desain: untuk spesies Acropora dan Diplopora, kombinasi permukaan berpori, tekstur mikroskopis aktif, dan ion bermanfaat (Ca, Sr, Si) dapat meningkatkan penyerapan larva dan awal mineralisasi. <cite id="c9f6a97a-2">Substrates with specific inorganic additives positively responded to soluble inorganic minerals such as silica and strontianite</cite> <cite id="c9f6a97a-4">Preference for quartz sand may result from surface features or silicate release into the water column</cite>.

Kelebihan substrat buatan dibanding substrat alami
- Ketersediaan dan kontrol lingkungan awal: substrat alami seringkali rusak (rubble), datar, dan tidak stabil; substrat buatan menawarkan permukaan penyangga, menangkap fragment, dan mempercepat pertumbuhan di lingkungan berdeposisi. <cite id="e6fdab59-0">Rubble becomes a ‘killing field’ for juveniles; artificial substrates are used for transplantation and recruitment</cite> <cite id="e6fdab59-4">Mesh/sloping substrata mitigate sediment accumulation and support faster growth</cite>.
- Kapasitas nursery dan biodiversitas: substrat buatan berfungsi sebagai kantung pertumbuhan dan habitat sementara bagi komunitas laut, meningkatkan keanekaragaman dan fungsi ekosistem. <cite id="e6fdab59-1">Coral nurseries on artificial substrates promote coral growth and provide habitat for marine life, increasing fish aggregation and biodiversity</cite> <cite id="e6fdab59-4">Artificial substrates developed via natural colonization can be enhanced by transplantation, serving as microhabitats that enhance biodiversity</cite>.
- Aplikasi spesifik di daerah marginal/terdegradasi: substrat buatan mudah diadaptasi di pantai/terumbu marginal dan di sekitar proyek reklamasi dengan sedimentasi tinggi. <cite id="8eadc85e-0">Artificial substrates are studied to compose artificial reefs for restoration at marginal reef conditions</cite> <cite id="e6fdab59-4">Restoration techniques overcoming sedimentation challenges are viable, using sloping solid substrata and horizontal mesh surfaces</cite>.

Keterbatasan dan risiko substrat buatan
- Biaya, daya tahan, dan ekologi: beton/ semen umumnya mahal dan memerlukan teknik khusus, sementara bahan alternatif perlu uji lapangan; substrat buatan mungkin tidak sepenuhnya meniru interaksi ekologis alami, struktur kompleksitas, dan daya tahan jangka panjang. <cite id="e6fdab59-0">Most artificial substrates are expensive and based on land-based materials like concrete/cement; modified coral rubble with nets provides a low-cost alternative needing further testing</cite> <cite id="e6fdab59-1">Artificial substrates may present limitations including ecological interaction differences, structural complexity changes, and long-term stability/durability issues compared to natural reefs</cite>.
- Ketergantungan pada spesies dan teknik pemasangan: pertumbuhan dan kelangsungan karang di substrat buatan bisa berbeda antar spesies; metode pemasangan (kabel tie vs epoxy) dan orientasi fragmen memengaruhi keberhasilan; substrat dasar (level terendah) sering tertutup pasir. <cite id="e6fdab59-2">Cable tie method is effective and comparable to epoxy or cement for Acropora; lower levels often covered by sediment, so transplantation avoided there</cite> <cite id="e6fdab59-3">Artificial substrates may not fully replicate conditions necessary for growth and survival of certain coral species</cite>.
- Kimia bahan dan leaching: bahan seperti logam dan plastik mungkin melepas ion/ zat kimia yang memengaruhi larva dan komunitas perifiton; desain berbasis kapur dengan aditif mineral menunjukkan bahwa ion tertentu dapat merangsang penempelan, tetapi risiko toksisitas bahan kimia perlu dikaji. <cite id="c9f6a97a-1">Larval settlement is influenced by material properties; settlement-inducing algae and microbial communities on different materials have been assessed</cite> <cite id="c9f6a97a-3">Soluble additives (SrCO3, SiO2) can release ions that influence larval settlement; material composition is critical</cite>.
- Monitoring jangka panjang: keterikatan biologis dan dinamika komunitas di substrat buatan perlu pengawasan untuk memastikan tidak terjadi dominasi oleh alga, organisme kompetitor, atau penyakit yang merugikan karang. <cite id="e6fdab59-1">Continued monitoring and research are essential to assess long-term effectiveness and sustainability</cite>.

Panduan praktis pemilihan dan pelaksanaan substrat buatan
- Pemilihan bahan:
  • Lingkungan berdeposisi: pilih permukaan datar bergradien (drop-off) dan mesh terbuka untuk mengurangi penumpukan pasir, atau kombinasinya. <cite id="e6fdab59-4">Sloping solid substrata and horizontal mesh surfaces prevent sediment accumulation</cite>.
  • Akses lokal dan biaya: pertimbangkan struktur dari koral runtuhan yang dikemas dengan jaring lokal untuk biaya rendah dan adaptasi situs. <cite id="e6fdab59-0">Modified coral rubble with cheap locally available nets successfully replaced concrete as transplantation media with growing corals</cite>.
  • Spesies sasaran: untuk Acropora dan Diplopora, evaluasi substrat kapur dengan aditif CaCO3 dan ion Sr/Si untuk meningkatkan penempelan awal. <cite id="c9f6a97a-2">Additives such as silica and strontianite were positively responded to by larvae in choice experiments</cite>.
- Desain permukaan:
  • Buat pori/tekstur berukuran mikron–milimeter untuk menunjang keselektifan larva dan penambatan awal, sambil menjaga permeabilitas air. <cite id="c9f6a97a-3">Larvae detect localized topographical features smaller than body width and show species-specific preferences</cite>.
- Teknik pemasangan:
  • Gunakan kabel tie, epoxy, atau semen berdasarkan sasaran spesies dan konteks; kabel tie sudah terbukti efektif dan setara dengan bahan kimia. <cite id="e6fdab59-2">Cable ties widely applied and effective; similar effective to epoxy or cement for attaching Acropora fragments</cite>.
  • Hindari menempatkan fragmen di lapisan paling bawah struktur bertingkat yang rawan endapan pasir. <cite id="e6fdab59-2">Transplantation was avoided at the base level due to sediment resuspension covering the substrate</cite>.
- Monitoring dan penyesuaian:
  • Evaluasi pertumbuhan bulanan, mortalitas, dan kompetisi alga/organisme; sesuaikan rasio lapisan substrat (atas/menengah/atas) dan rotasi fragmen untuk distribusi cahaya dan nutrisi. <cite id="e6fdab59-1">Artificial substrates may differ in ecological interactions and structural complexity; long-term monitoring is essential</cite>.

Contoh penerapan di Indonesia
- Program di Padang (Sumatra Barat): kolaborasi antara substrat buatan dan transplantasi karang melalui CSR Pertamina menunjukkan substrat buatan tumbuh biota perifiton dan invertebrata, meningkatkan recruitment karang (percent cover dari 1,33% → 2,19%), peningkatan keberadaan ikan, dan fungsi sebagai ground fishing. <cite id="8eadc85e-1">Artificial reef structures were colonized by biofouling and small sponges; recruitment increased from 1.33% to 2.19% cover; fish aggregation increased, including high-value species and schools of golden trevally</cite>.
- Eksperimen substrat di Pantai Panjang (Java): multilevel concrete APR dengan teknik pemasangan kabel tie mendukung pertumbuhan Acropora aspera dan copiosa; penempatan di level atas/menengah untuk menghindari gangguan fisik dan endapan. <cite id="e6fdab59-2">Transplantation on multilevel concrete APR with cable ties supported growth of Acropora species; base level avoided due to sediment resuspension</cite>.
- Alternatif lokal dan ekonomis: di Seribu, substrat dari koral runtuhan dikemas jaring nylon/PE menawarkan biaya rendah, kompleksitas permukaan, dan stabilitas yang cukup untuk pertumbuhan karang; perlu pengujian di lokasi dan waktu yang lebih panjang. <cite id="e6fdab59-0">Modified coral rubble with nets provided a low-cost, locally available alternative to concrete, supporting coral growth and requiring further site testing</cite>.
- Diversitas ikan di substrat buatan vs alami: di Bulukumba, substrat karang mati berbentuk branching/tabulate menarik komunitas ikan yang setara dengan substrat hidup untuk spesies major/indikator/target; pecahan karang dominan target dan indikator, menunjukkan substrat buatan bisa menyerap komunitas laut khasik. <cite id="8eadc85e-2">Substrat branching/tabulate dan karang hidup menunjukkan proporsi spesies major/indikator/target yang setara; substrat karang mati dan pecahan dominan target/indikator</cite>.
- Rekruitmen karang di lingkungan stabil: di Bunaken (Manado), 90% juvenil menempel pada substrat stabil (hidup/blok), 10% pada rubble, menegaskan bahwa substrat stabil meningkatkan peluang awal tumbuh karang. <cite id="8eadc85e-3">Density of recruitments was 8.43 colonies/m²; 90% settlement on stable substrata and 10% on unstable rubble</cite>.

Pertimbangan khusus di lingkungan sedimentaria dan kota
- Dalam daerah dekat pembersihan pantai, reklamasi, atau aliran pasir, substrat buatan dirancang agar tidak memperparah penumpukan pasir; gunakan gradien curam dan mesh terbuka di nursery dan lokasi outplanting. <cite id="e6fdab59-4">Restoration techniques that overcome sedimentation challenges are viable, including sloping solid substrata and horizontal mesh surfaces</cite>.
- Di lingkungan beroksigen rendah, pertimbangkan permukaan berpori dan bahan ringan (koral runtuhan+mesh) yang mempercepat difusi air dan mengurangi risiko asfiksia fragment. <cite id="e6fdab59-0">Stability and complexity of surface created by nets make the substrate suitable for coral transplantation with local economic benefits</cite>.

Bagaimana memilih substrat buatan sesuai spesies karang sasaran
- Untuk spesies riam/rambut (Acropora, Pocillopora), prioritaskan substrat berbasis kapur dengan aditif kimiawi yang mendukung mineralisasi awal dan permukaan mikroaktif; kombinasikan dengan teknik pemasangan kabel tie dan orientasi miring terhadap aliran air. <cite id="c9f6a97a-2">Larvae responded positively to soluble inorganic minerals such as silica and strontianite in composite calcium carbonate substrates</cite> <cite id="e6fdab59-2">Cable ties effective and comparable to epoxy/cement for Acropora; orientation and fixation matter</cite>.
- Untuk spesies besar/kuantum (massive/tabulate), gunakan permukaan datar berpori besar dan lapisan bertingkat agar menempel di bagian atas struktur; hindari area dasar yang rawan pasir. <cite id="e6fdab59-2">Upper and middle levels used for transplanting to prevent physical damage and sedimentation at the base</cite>.
- Untuk restorasi rantai makanan dan biodiversitas, pasang substrat beragam bentuk (branching, tabulate, massive) dan gabungkan dengan vegetasi alga perifiton yang stabil untuk menarik herbivora dan planktivora. <cite id="8eadc85e-2">Substrat branching/tabulate supported comparable fish diversity to live coral; recruitment patterns varied by substrate type</cite>.

Sumber daya dan bacaan lanjutan
- Studi lapangan dan uji substrat: <cite id="e6fdab59-0">Artificial substrates for transplantation and recruitment; modified coral rubble with nets as low-cost alternative</cite> <cite id="e6fdab59-1">Coral nursery on artificial substrates in Lakshadweep with ecological caveats and monitoring needs</cite> <cite id="e6fdab59-2">Transplantation on concrete APRs with cable ties; level design and sediment avoidance</cite> <cite id="e6fdab59-3">Testing natural vs artificial substrates; typical materials (ceramic, concrete, terracotta) and species-specific needs</cite> <cite id="e6fdab59-4">Designing solid and mesh substrata to overcome sedimentation; nursery effects 3–5× faster growth</cite>.
- Mekanisme larva dan desain kimia: <cite id="c9f6a97a-0">Engineered substrates reveal species-specific inorganic cues; larvae distinguish materials independent of mean roughness/wettability</cite> <cite id="c9f6a97a-1">Composite substrates from CaCO3 with sands/glasses/alkaline-earth carbonates reveal additive-specific preferences</cite> <cite id="c9f6a97a-2">Larvae detect micro-scale topography and respond positively to silica and strontianite</cite> <cite id="c9f6a97a-3">Ion release from SrCO3 and SiO2 additives implicated in settlement; material composition critical</cite> <cite id="c9f6a97a-4">Specificity and possible silicate release mechanisms for quartz sand preference</cite>.
- Aplikasi lokal di Indonesia: <cite id="8eadc85e-0">Biofilm succession on artificial substrates for artificial reef development in marginal reefs</cite> <cite id="8eadc85e-1">Collaboration of artificial reefs and transplantation in Padang improved fish aggregation and recruitment cover</cite> <cite id="8eadc85e-2">Fish assemblages on different substrate shapes, including dead coral forms and live coral, show comparable diversity</cite> <cite id="8eadc85e-3">Recruitment density and settlement preference on stable vs unstable substrata in Molas, Manado</cite>.

Kesimpulan
- Substrat buatan adalah fondasi kritis dalam transplantasi karang modern, memberikan permukaan stabil, porositas, dan lingkungan awal yang dikontrol untuk pertumbuhan dan rekruitmen karang di habitat terdegradasi. <cite id="e6fdab59-0">Artificial substrates are used both for transplantation and recruitment</cite> <cite id="e6fdab59-1">They promote coral growth and habitat provision but require long-term monitoring</cite>.
- Pemilihan bahan dan desain harus disesuaikan dengan dinamika pasir, spesies karang, dan mekanisme pilihan substrat larva; desain berbasis kapur dengan aditif mineral dan permukaan mikroaktif dapat meningkatkan penempelan awal, sementara teknik pemasangan dan orientasi fragmen perlu optimalisasi di lapangan. <cite id="c9f6a97a-2">Additive-specific settlement preferences and micro-scale recognition inform material design</cite> <cite id="e6fdab59-2">Cable-tie fixation and tiered placement mitigate physical damage and sedimentation</cite>.
- Di Indonesia, berbagai program menunjukkan substrat buatan dapat meningkatkan recruitment karang, menarik komunitas ikan, dan berfungsi sebagai habitat alternatif, tetapi keberhasilan jangka panjang bergantung pada desain yang sesuai dan pengawasan lingkungan setempat. <cite id="8eadc85e-1">Reef structures supported recruitment increase and fish aggregation in Padang</cite> <cite id="e6fdab59-0">Low-cost modified coral rubble substrates with nets support coral growth and local adaptation</cite>.
</answer>

Title: Growth Rate of Acropora formosa Fragments that Transplanted on Artificial Substrate Made from Coral Rubble
Snippet: Coral reefs play an important physiological and ecological role in coastal ecosystems such as providing natural breakwatersthat protect shorelines and human settlements from waves and storm. Corals killed by tsunami, waves and storms are often degraded into rubble. This rubble is dynamic, easily shifted by currents and storms, which effectively forms â€˜â€˜killing fieldsâ€™â€™ forcoral juveniles, hindering coral recovery. In order to rehabilitate coral reefs, artificial substrates are used both for coral transplantation and recruitment. Unfortunately, most artificial substrates are expensive and use land-based material such asconcrete/cement-bases. In order to develop a new low-cost artificial substrate that can replace concrete/cement-base as amedia for coral transplantation, modified coral rubble was tested in a pilot study in Seribu Island, Jakarta. Two different nets (nylon and polyethylene) were used to form rubble into a compact shape, stable and strong substrate. The stability of therubble and the complexity of the surface which is created by the net make this substrate suitable for coral transplantation.Additionally, from an economic perspective the nets are very cheap and locally available. In a number of experiments,modified coral rubble successfully replaced the concrete /cement-base as a media for coral transplantation. The coral transplants were growing over time. With this method, we can try to rehabilitate the degraded coral reef destroyed by tsunami or other factors with material that already is available at the site and with less money. However, this approach requires testing at additional sites and for longer periods, to determine the replicability of the results.Key words: cement base, coral, rubble, transplantation

Title: Successful establishment of a coral nursery for active reef restoration in Kavaratti Island, Lakshadweep archipelago
Snippet: The coral transplantation on artificial substrates in the shallow lagoon off the Lakshadweep archipelago has shown promising results in establishing a coral nursery, promoting coral growth and providing a habitat for marine life. The establishment of a coral nursery has led to increased fish aggregation, contributing to enhanced biodiversity and ecosystem resilience. These findings highlight the potential of this restoration technique as a valuable tool in reef conservation efforts for vulnerable ecosystems such as those found in the Lakshadweep archipelago. However, the use of artificial substrates instead of transplanting corals directly onto degraded reefs may present certain limitations, such as differences in the ecological interactions between the artificial and natural environments, potential changes in the structural complexity, and the long-term stability and durability of the artificial substrates. Additionally, the artificial substrates may not fully replicate the conditions necessary for the growth and survival of certain coral species. Continued monitoring and research are essential to assess the long-term effectiveness and sustainability of this approach.

Title: Coral transplantation on a multilevel substrate of Artificial Patch Reefs: effect of fixing methods on the growth rate of two Acropora species
Snippet: Coral fragments were collected from donor site of two Acropora species in the inner lagoon and in front of the reef flat of Panjang Island. Fragments of A. aspera were collected by broken off small branches at random mother colonies while A. copiosa fragments were chisel off main branches of adult colonies randomly. The small branches of two species (average size was 12.57 cm 3 ) were transferred into basket and then were transplanted on multilevel substrates of Artificial Patch Reefs (APR) which deployed in the eastern site of Panjang Island. Artificial Patch Reefs (APR) is artificial reefs made by concrete blocks composed as modular circular structures in shape, constructed 5 (five) levels of substrates were deployed from small boats by SCUBA divers, and are suitable near natural reefs in shallow water. The total height of the multilevel APR structure is about 120 cm from the bottom of the sea, and the height of each level is 20 cm. In this experiment, coral fragments were transplanted in the upper, middle, and lower level. Coral transplantation experiments were not applied at the top level to prevent physical damage in coral fragments. The experiments were also not implemented in the coral transplantation in the base of APR (level 5) since the surface of the substrate usually covering sediment due to resuspension (Figure 2). At the beginning of November 2018, 120 coral fragments were transplanted on three levels of APR by two fixation methods: vertically and horizontally orientation of the fragments fixing on the surface of substrates and tied to a paired of the nail using cable ties (Figure 3). Cable ties method of coral transplantation has been widely applied and effective technique for attaching Acropora fragments to artificial substrate (William and Miller 2010;Young et al. 2012). Coral fragment stabilization using cable ties was similarly effective to epoxy or cement methods (William and Miller 2010).

Title: Testing the effectiveness of natural and artificial substrates for coral reef restoration at Isla Isabel National Park, Mexico
Snippet: Scleractinian corals are the main engineers of coral reef ecosystems, due to their capacity to precipitate calcium carbonate (CaCO 3 ), forming tridimensional structures that constitute the base of the physical reef-framework and providing ecosystem services and habitat to associated biodiversity (Álvarez-Filip et al., 2009;Sheppard et al., 2010). Coral reef ecosystems have been threatened by natural events (heatwaves, hurricanes, diseases, and others), and human-derived activities (coastaldevelopment, nutrient input, overfishing, and marine pollution), causing large coral mortality (up to 50 %) in Eastern Tropical Pacific (ETP) over the last three decades (De'ath et al., 2009;Rinkevich, 2015). As natural recovery occurs slowly (decades or centuries), many active restoration tools have emerged as an alternative strategy to accelerate coral recovery and mitigate the rapid coral reef degradation (Rinkevich, 2020). Direct coral transplantation is one of the most used techniques as it avoids the early-stage of coral farming/nursering and post-outplanting stress, which have resulted in high survival and growth rates (Harriott & Fisk, 1988;Tortolero-Langarica et al., 2014). Also, artificial substrate (typically comprised of ceramic, concrete, or terracotta, among others) is most likely to aid in reef conservation and restoration by providing nursery habitat for target species or recruitment substrate for corals and other organisms (Hylkema et al., 2021; Introducción: Los corales ramificados del género Pocillopora son los constructores arrecifales más importantes del Pacífico Tropical Oriental (PTO). Sin embargo, sus poblaciones han disminuido por efectos de eventos de estrés térmico ocurridos las últimas décadas. Por ello, se han desarrollado estrategias de restauración activa como respuesta de mitigación, pero no ha sido posible establecer protocolos específicos para estas especies en el PTO.

Title: Enhancing Marine Biodiversity in Singapore’s Urbanizing Coastal Environment
Snippet: The loss of more than half of coral reef habitats to land reclamation and the exposure of the remaining reefs to chronic sedimentation necessitate active restoration interventions. This will complement the observed natural colonization by corals on seawalls and other structures along modified shores [29], [30]. Reef restoration efforts employing techniques that overcome sedimentation challenges have been demonstrated to be viable [31], [32]. These range from the provision of sloping solid substrata [33] or horizontal mesh surfaces that prevent sediment accumulation [34]. 

In-situ coral nurseries (Fig. 2) have a significant role in reef restoration efforts in a sediment-challenged environment [35]. Studies on two scleractinian species, Pachyseris speciosa and Pocillopora acuta (previously damicornis) [36], indicated that fragments raised in nurseries for five months before being transplanted to the reef substrate, grew significantly faster by three to five times compared to those that were transplanted directly without a nursery phase [37]. The faster growth of transplants in nurseries augmented their size and continued to manifest after they were transplanted to the reef, enabling them to perform better than the directly transplanted fragments. 

The coral nurseries themselves also served as microhabitats to enhance biodiversity despite the sedimentation, attracting a large variety of species such as fishes [38] and reef-associated invertebrates [39]. These nurseries also provided opportunities for recruitment, settlement and development of reef fauna. They enhance ecosystem functioning in degraded or non-reefal sites while at the same time nurture coral fragments for transplantation [32]. 

The biodiversity of artificial substrates developed through natural colonization can be enhanced by active transplantation particularly in the intertidal zone. Natural colonization shows the viability of hard structures such as seawalls as habitats for biological communities [40] and transplantation can further enhance the structure's ecological value. Fragments of five species of scleractinian corals, three species of soft corals and three species of sponges reared in ex-situ nurseries prior to transplantation exhibited variable survivorship and growth.

snippet.text:
The loss of more than half of coral reef habitats to land reclamation and the exposure of the remaining reefs to chronic sedimentation necessitate active restoration interventions. This will complement the observed natural colonization by corals on seawalls and other structures along modified shores [29], [30]. Reef restoration efforts employing techniques that overcome sedimentation challenges have been demonstrated to be viable [31], [32]. These range from the provision of sloping solid substrata [33] or horizontal mesh surfaces that prevent sediment accumulation [34]. 

In-situ coral nurseries (Fig. 2) have a significant role in reef restoration efforts in a sediment-challenged environment [35]. Studies on two scleractinian species, Pachyseris speciosa and Pocillopora acuta (previously damicornis) [36], indicated that fragments raised in nurseries for five months before being transplanted to the reef substrate, grew significantly faster by three to five times compared to those that were transplanted directly without a nursery phase [37]. The faster growth of transplants in nurseries augmented their size and continued to manifest after they were transplanted to the reef, enabling them to perform better than the directly transplanted fragments. 

The coral nurseries themselves also served as microhabitats to enhance biodiversity despite the sedimentation, attracting a large variety of species such as fishes [38] and reef-associated invertebrates [39]. These nurseries also provided opportunities for recruitment, settlement and development of reef fauna. They enhance ecosystem functioning in degraded or non-reefal sites while at the same time nurture coral fragments for transplantation [32]. 

The biodiversity of artificial substrates developed through natural colonization can be enhanced by active transplantation particularly in the intertidal zone. Natural colonization shows the viability of hard structures such as seawalls as habitats for biological communities [40] and transplantation can further enhance the structure's ecological value. Fragments of five species of scleractinian corals, three species of soft corals and three species of sponges reared in ex-situ nurseries prior to transplantation exhibited variable survivorship and growth.

documents.title: Growth Rate of Acropora formosa Fragments that Transplanted on Artificial Substrate Made from Coral Rubble
documents.snippet: Coral reefs play an important physiological and ecological role in coastal ecosystems such as providing natural breakwatersthat protect shorelines and human settlements from waves and storm. Corals killed by tsunami, waves and storms are often degraded into rubble. This rubble is dynamic, easily shifted by currents and storms, which effectively forms â€˜â€˜killing fieldsâ€™â€™ forcoral juveniles, hindering coral recovery. In order to rehabilitate coral reefs, artificial substrates are used both for coral transplantation and recruitment. Unfortunately, most artificial substrates are expensive and use land-based material such asconcrete/cement-bases. In order to develop a new low-cost artificial substrate that can replace concrete/cement-base as amedia for coral transplantation, modified coral rubble was tested in a pilot study in Seribu Island, Jakarta. Two different nets (nylon and polyethylene) were used to form rubble into a compact shape, stable and strong substrate. The stability of therubble and the complexity of the surface which is created by the net make this substrate suitable for coral transplantation.Additionally, from an economic perspective the nets are very cheap and locally available. In a number of experiments,modified coral rubble successfully replaced the concrete /cement-base as a media for coral transplantation. The coral transplants were growing over time. With this method, we can try to rehabilitate the degraded coral reef destroyed by tsunami or other factors with material that already is available at the site and with less money. However, this approach requires testing at additional sites and for longer periods, to determine the replicability of the results.Key words: cement base, coral, rubble, transplantation

documents.title: Successful establishment of a coral nursery for active reef restoration in Kavaratti Island, Lakshadweep archipelago
documents.snippet: The coral transplantation on artificial substrates in the shallow lagoon off the Lakshadweep archipelago has shown promising results in establishing a coral nursery, promoting coral growth and providing a habitat for marine life. The establishment of a coral nursery has led to increased fish aggregation, contributing to enhanced biodiversity and ecosystem resilience. These findings highlight the potential of this restoration technique as a valuable tool in reef conservation efforts for vulnerable ecosystems such as those found in the Lakshadweep archipelago. However, the use of artificial substrates instead of transplanting corals directly onto degraded reefs may present certain limitations, such as differences in the ecological interactions between the artificial and natural environments, potential changes in the structural complexity, and the long-term stability and durability of the artificial substrates. Additionally, the artificial substrates may not fully replicate the conditions necessary for the growth and survival of certain coral species. Continued monitoring and research are essential to assess the long-term effectiveness and sustainability of this approach.

documents.title: Coral transplantation on a multilevel substrate of Artificial Patch Reefs: effect of fixing methods on the growth rate of two Acropora species
documents.snippet: Coral fragments were collected from donor site of two Acropora species in the inner lagoon and in front of the reef flat of Panjang Island. Fragments of A. aspera were collected by broken off small branches at random mother colonies while A. copiosa fragments were chisel off main branches of adult colonies randomly. The small branches of two species (average size was 12.57 cm 3 ) were transferred into basket and then were transplanted on multilevel substrates of Artificial Patch Reefs (APR) which deployed in the eastern site of Panjang Island. Artificial Patch Reefs (APR) is artificial reefs made by concrete blocks composed as modular circular structures in shape, constructed 5 (five) levels of substrates were deployed from small boats by SCUBA divers, and are suitable near natural reefs in shallow water. The total height of the multilevel APR structure is about 120 cm from the bottom of the sea, and the height of each level is 20 cm. In this experiment, coral fragments were transplanted in the upper, middle, and lower level. Coral transplantation experiments were not applied at the top level to prevent physical damage in coral fragments. The experiments were also not implemented in the coral transplantation in the base of APR (level 5) since the surface of the substrate usually covering sediment due to resuspension (Figure 2). At the beginning of November 2018, 120 coral fragments were transplanted on three levels of APR by two fixation methods: vertically and horizontally orientation of the fragments fixing on the surface of substrates and tied to a paired of the nail using cable ties (Figure 3). Cable ties method of coral transplantation has been widely applied and effective technique for attaching Acropora fragments to artificial substrate (William and Miller 2010;Young et al. 2012). Coral fragment stabilization using cable ties was similarly effective to epoxy or cement methods (William and Miller 2010).

Title: Engineered Substrates Reveal Species-Specific Inorganic Cues for Coral Larval Settlement
Snippet: 0] The operational term for this process is "coral larval recruitment." During the process of coral reproduction and recruitment, corals first release either swimming larvae or gametes that develop into larvae. 9][20] Researchers and restoration practitioners routinely harness these cues to induce larval settlement in the laboratory.  Once larvae have settled and matured into juvenile corals over several weeks to months in protected aquaria or nurseries, they are then outplanted back to degraded reefs to bolster restoration efforts. 

Although not yet routinely applied by coral restoration practitioners, there are also many physical cues that can influence the behavior of marine larvae. 3] Some studies have also reported settlement preferences based on substrate color 22,44 or wettability. 39,45  owever, like studies of surface roughness, these studies have focused on extrinsic and/or bulk (average) properties of the substrate rather than the intrinsic properties of the underlying material. 

As reef-building organisms, corals are complex arrangements of both soft organic tissues and hard bioinorganic skeletons. Thus, it is plausible that corals have evolved to seek out specific inorganic chemicals or materials during the larval stage that would indicate whether a location will be favorable for mineralization and skeletal attachment and support. 9] However, to our knowledge, larval settlement cues related solely to inorganic material composition have not yet been investigated systematically. 

Here, we present the development of artificial substrates containing potential inorganic larval settlement cues and the discovery of species-specific settlement preferences in the absence of CCA or other biochemical settlement inducers. We produced lime mortar (CaCO3) substrates with a range of additivesincluding sands, glasses, and carbonates of alkaline earth elements that are essential to coral mineralization-to determine whether larvae exhibit preferences to settle on particular materials. In randomized settlement choice experiments with larvae of the Caribbean elkhorn coral Acropora palmata and grooved brain coral Diploria labyrinthiformis, larvae distinguished between substrates containing different inorganic additives and different concentrations of a glass fiber additive. Analysis of substrate properties using 3D laser scanning confocal microscopy and direct contact angle measurements revealed no correlation between settlement preference and average surface roughness or wettability. Instead, our results support the existence of more localized surface recognition capabilities in coral larvae.

Title: Composite Substrates Reveal Inorganic Material Cues for Coral Larval Settlement
Snippet: : The widespread loss of stony reef-building coral populations has been compounded by the low settlement and survival of coral juveniles. To rebuild coral communities, restoration practitioners have developed work ﬂ ows to settle vulnerable coral larvae in the laboratory and outplant settled juveniles back to natural and arti ﬁ cial reefs. These work ﬂ ows often make use of natural biochemical settlement cues, which are presented to swimming larvae to induce settlement. This paper establishes the potential for inorganic cues to complement these known biochemical e ﬀ ects. Settlement substrates were fabricated from calcium carbonate, a material present naturally on reefs, and modi ﬁ ed with additives including sands, glasses, and alkaline earth carbonates. Experiments with larvae of two Caribbean coral species revealed additive-speci ﬁ c settlement preferences that were independent of bulk surface properties such as mean roughness and wettability. Instead, analyses of the substrates suggest that settling coral larvae can detect localized topographical features more than an order of magnitude smaller than their body width and can sense and positively respond to soluble inorganic minerals such as silica (SiO 2 ) and strontianite (SrCO 3 ). Although not yet routinely applied by coral restoration practitioners, there are also many physical cues that can influence the behavior of marine larvae. 3] Some studies have also reported settlement preferences based on substrate color 22,44 or wettability. 39,45  owever, like studies of surface roughness, these studies have focused on extrinsic and/or bulk (average) properties of the substrate rather than the intrinsic properties of the underlying material. 

As reef-building organisms, corals are complex arrangements of both soft organic tissues and hard bioinorganic skeletons. Thus, it is plausible that corals have evolved to seek out specific inorganic chemicals or materials during the larval stage that would indicate whether a location will be favorable for mineralization and skeletal attachment and support. 9] However, to our knowledge, larval settlement cues related solely to inorganic material composition have not yet been investigated systematically. 

Here, we present the development of artificial substrates containing potential inorganic larval settlement cues and the discovery of species-specific settlement preferences in the absence of CCA or other biochemical settlement inducers. We produced lime mortar (CaCO3) substrates with a range of additivesincluding sands, glasses, and carbonates of alkaline earth elements that are essential to coral mineralization-to determine whether larvae exhibit preferences to settle on particular materials. In randomized settlement choice experiments with larvae of the Caribbean elkhorn coral Acropora palmata and grooved brain coral Diploria labyrinthiformis, larvae distinguished between substrates containing different inorganic additives and different concentrations of a glass fiber additive. Analysis of substrate properties using 3D laser scanning confocal microscopy and direct contact angle measurements revealed no correlation between settlement preference and average surface roughness or wettability. Instead, our results support the existence of more localized surface recognition capabilities in coral larvae.

documents.snippet: : The widespread loss of stony reef-building coral populations has been compounded by the low settlement and survival of coral juveniles. To rebuild coral communities, restoration practitioners have developed work ﬂ ows to settle vulnerable coral larvae in the laboratory and outplant settled juveniles back to natural and arti ﬁ cial reefs. These work ﬂ ows often make use of natural biochemical settlement cues, which are presented to swimming larvae to induce settlement. This paper establishes the potential for inorganic cues to complement these known biochemical e ﬀ ects. Settlement substrates were fabricated from calcium carbonate, a material present naturally on reefs, and modi ﬁ ed with additives including sands, glasses, and alkaline earth carbonates. Experiments with larvae of two Caribbean coral species revealed additive-speci ﬁ c settlement preferences that were independent of bulk surface properties such as mean roughness and wettability. Instead, analyses of the substrates suggest that settling coral larvae can detect localized topographical features more than an order of magnitude smaller than their body width and can sense and positively respond to soluble inorganic minerals such as silica (SiO 2 ) and strontianite (SrCO 3 ). These ﬁ ndings open a new area of research in coral reef restoration, in which composite substrates can be designed with a combination of natural organic and inorganic additives to increase larval settlement and perhaps also improve post-settlement growth, mineralization, and defense. of the lime mortar fabrication process and the fabrication of additional substrate types are provided in the Supporting Information along with details on substrate characterization methods.
