Snippet: AbstrakKajian ini ditujukan untuk mengeksplorasi capaian pelaksanaan rehabilitasi terumbu karang melalui kolaborasi terumbu buatan dan transplantasi karang di Kecamatan Bungus Teluk Kabung Kota Padang. Program ini diinisisasi oleh CSR PT. PERTAMINA (Persero) MOR I – Teluk Kabung berlandaskan fakta bahwa kondisi terumbu karang di daerah ini mulai mengalami degradasi lingkungan yang diakibatkan oleh perubahan alam dan ulah tangan manusia yang tidak bertanggung jawab. Metode yang digunakan pada program ini dilihat dari 2 aspek, yaitu pembuatan media substrat dan pengambilan biofisik sebagai pendukung ekologi manfaat terumbu buatan. Hasil rehabilitasi terumbu karang melalui kolaborasi terumbu buatan dan transplantasi karang menunjukkan beberapa hal, antara lain: (1) terumbu buatan banyak ditumbuhi biota lainnya seperti, biofulling dan teritip dan lili laut; (2) di sekitar terumbu buatan, dijumpai rekuitment karang-karang yang mulai berkembang dengan ukuran yang masih kecil dan meningkat percent covernya dari 1,33% menjadi 2,19%; (3) keberadaan ikan pada terumbu buatan semakin meningkat; dan (4) terumbu buatan dihuni oleh ikan-ikan berekonomis tinggi seperti kerapu,bibir tebal, dan sering dijumpai gerombolan ikan ekor kuning sehingga tujuan utama terumbu buatan terpenuhi yaitu sebagai fishing ground masyarakat di

Title: Potensi Ekosistem Terumbu Karang untuk Pengembangan Ekowisata di Pulau Noko Bawean
Snippet: Terumbu karang dikenal sebagai organisme laut yang berkelompok dan dapat bertumbuh serta berkembang biak, dimana habitatnya biasa ditemui di dasar laut yang dangkal. Terumbu karang memiliki potensi yang dapat dimanfaatkan baik bagi ekosistem laut, maupun bagi masyarakat yang berada di wilayah pesisir. Manfaat terumbu karang bagi masyarakat pesisir yaitu berperan dalam hasil tangkapan ikan oleh para nelayan, selain itu juga dengan terjaganya terumbu karang dapat menarik wisatawan untuk pergi berlibur dan secara langsung mampu menaikkan perekonomian masyarakat pesisir. Terlebih lagi Indonesia terus mempromosikan wisata berbasis alam atau biasa disebut ekowisata. Adanya ketertarikan akan potensi ekosistem terumbu karang terhadap perkembangan ekowisata menjadi alasan dilakukannya penelitian ini. Pulau Noko yang terletak di Dusun Gili Desa Sidogedungbatu Kecamatan Sangkapura Kabupaten Gresik dipilih untuk menadi lokasi penelitian. Tujuan diadakannya penelitian ini untuk mengetahui potensi ekosistem terumbu karang di Pulau Noko. Metode yang digunakan dalam penelitian ini berasal dari study litelature, observasi dan wawancara. Hasil dari penelitian ini menunjukan bahwa terumbu karang yang terdapat di Pulau Noko berasal dari alam dan transplatasi buatan. Teknik stationary visual censusdiaplikasikan untuk mendata ikan pada 4 bentuk substrat karang mati (masif, branching, tabulate, pecahan karang mati, dan karang alami/hidup sebagai kontrol). Luas area pengamatan sebesar 2x2 m2 dan dilakukan 5 kali pengulangan untuk setiap substrat.. Perbandingan jumlah jenis dan kepadatan ikan antara substrat dilakukan dengan analisis ragam dan sebaran spasial dengan analisis koresponden. Ditemukan proporsi yang setara untuk ikan major, indikator, dan target pada substrat branching, tabulate dan karang hidup. Substrat karang mati, didominasi oleh ikan target dan ikan indikator. Sedangkan pada substrat berupa pecahan karang mati didominasi oleh kelompok ikan major dan target. Komposisi individu didominasi oleh ikan indikator, kecuali pada substrat pecahan karang, didominasi oleh ikan target. Pada substrat dengan bentuk branching memiliki kekayaan spesies dan kepadatan ikan yang lebih tinggi dibandingkan dengan pecahan karang, namun tidak berbeda nyata dengan substrat karang tabulate dan karang alami.Sebaran spasial ikan indikator (famili Chaetodontidae) banyak ditemukan di substrat karang hidup, sedangkan pada substrat pecahan karang dicirikan oleh tingginya kepadatan ikan Acanthurus pyropherus, Arothron mappa,

documents.title: Study Of Hard Coral (Scleractinia) Recruitment In The Molas Waters, Manado City
documents.snippet: adalah masuknya individu karang baru pada populasi terumbu karang dikarenakan reproduksi ataupun migrasi.  Juvenil karang merupakan bentuk hasil metamorphosis dan pertumbuhan planula karang yang berukuran ≤ 5 cm dan menempel pada substrat tertentu.  Terdapat dua tipe substrat di perairan, substrat yang stabil dan substrat yang tidak stabil seperti pecahan karang (rubble).  Tujuan penelitian ini adalah untuk mempelajari tentang rekruitmen karang keras, baik dari densitas, komposisi jenis koloni juvenil karang, ukuran, hingga tipe substrat yang ditempati oleh juvenil karang.  Penelitian ini dilakukan pada bulan Agustus 2021 di perairan Molas Kecamatan Bunaken Kota Manado.  Metode yang digunakan untuk pemilihan lokasi adalah metode purposive sampling dan pengumpulan data menggunakan metode sampling dengan transek kuadran.  Hasil penelitian menunjukan bahwa densitas rekruitmen karang pada lokasi penelitian sebesar 8,43 koloni/m2.  Persentase penempelan juvenil karang pada substrat stabil sebesar 90% dan pada substrat yang tidak stabil sebesar 10%.  Ukuran rata-rata dari juvenil karang pada lokasi penelitian adalah 2,4cm.  Komposisi genus juvenil karang yang ditemukan pada lokasi penelitian adalah karang genus Acropora, Anacropora, Coeloseris, Cycloseris, Cyphastrea, Echinopora, Favites, Fungia, Galaxea, Goniastrea, Isopora, Leptastrea, Leptoseris,

documents.title: Potensi Ekosistem Terumbu Karang untuk Pengembangan Ekowisata di Pulau Noko Bawean
documents.snippet: Terumbu karang dikenal sebagai organisme laut yang berkelompok dan dapat bertumbuh serta berkembang biak, dimana habitatnya biasa ditemui di dasar laut yang dangkal. Terumbu karang memiliki potensi yang dapat dimanfaatkan baik bagi ekosistem laut, maupun bagi masyarakat yang berada di wilayah pesisir. Manfaat terumbu karang bagi masyarakat pesisir yaitu berperan dalam hasil tangkapan ikan oleh para nelayan, selain itu juga dengan terjaganya terumbu karang dapat menarik wisatawan untuk pergi berlibur dan secara langsung mampu menaikkan perekonomian masyarakat pesisir. Terlebih lagi Indonesia terus mempromosikan wisata berbasis alam atau biasa disebut ekowisata. Adanya ketertarikan akan potensi ekosistem terumbu karang terhadap perkembangan ekowisata menjadi alasan dilakukannya penelitian ini. Pulau Noko yang terletak di Dusun Gili Desa Sidogedungbatu Kecamatan Sangkapura Kabupaten Gresik dipilih untuk menadi lokasi penelitian. Tujuan diadakannya penelitian ini untuk mengetahui potensi ekosistem terumbu karang di Pulau Noko. Metode yang digunakan dalam penelitian ini berasal dari study litelature, observasi dan wawancara. Hasil dari penelitian ini menunjukan bahwa terumbu karang yang terdapat di Pulau Noko berasal dari alam dan transplatasi buatan. Terumbu karang yang terdapat di Pulau Noko berpotensi untuk menarik perhat

harder.brainstorming: The seed asks for artificial substrates in coral transplantation with sources. A straightforward survey would retrieve coral restoration literature and list substrate types (concrete, ceramic, etc.) with citations. To make this harder, I could: (1) require cross-domain synthesis that coral restoration papers don't explicitly make (engineering material properties vs ecological outcomes), (2) embed a temporal constraint forcing comparison across decades when methodology changed, (3) create a reasoning trap via conflating 'transplantation' (moving fragments) with 'larval settlement' (different substrate requirements), or (4) demand resolution of an implicit tradeoff that papers address separately but never directly compare. Option 3 is strongest: coral restoration literature discusses fragment attachment substrates and larval settlement substrates as distinct applications with different requirements, but the Indonesian phrasing 'transplantasi karang' is ambiguous. A system could retrieve both literatures and synthesize them without recognizing they answer different questions, or it must reason through which the question actually asks.
harder.chosen_strategy: Exploit technical ambiguity that maps to distinct research subfields: 'coral transplantation' conflates fragment transplantation (attaching adult fragments) versus larval recruitment (settlement substrates), which have contradictory substrate requirements that appear across separate literatures.
harder.updated_question: Substrat buatan apa yang paling efektif dalam transplantasi karang dewasa versus rekrutmen larva, dan mengapa persyaratannya bertentangan?
harder.why_harder: A survey can retrieve both fragment-attachment substrates (smooth, inert, stable) and larval-settlement substrates (rough, biofilm-rich, complex) and list their properties, but recognizing that these represent CONTRADICTORY requirements for different life stages requires reasoning about why texture/chemistry work oppositely in each context—something the literatures rarely make explicit because they address separate restoration goals.
harder.verification_criterion: The answer must cite sources addressing BOTH adult fragment attachment and larval settlement, explicitly state that their substrate requirements conflict in at least one property (e.g., surface roughness: fragments need smooth stable attachment points to prevent tissue damage, while larvae need rough microhabitats for settlement cues; or chemistry: inert materials for fragments vs biofilm-promoting materials for larvae), and explain the biological mechanism behind each opposing requirement. Fails if it lists substrates for only one life stage, treats the requirements as uniformly compatible, or does not explain WHY the same property (like roughness) has opposite effects.

attempts.answer:
Ringkasan
- Untuk rekrutmen larva, substrat buatan berbasis kalsium karbonat (batu bata/keramik CaCO3), semen/ beton, dan tanah liat terakota umumnya efektif meningkatkan penetapan larva, dengan beton cenderung menarik lebih banyak larva tetapi keragaman alga kompetitor yang tumbuh pada permukaan kasar dapat mengurangi kelangsungan hidup spata; komposit dengan sinyal anorganik (SiO2, SrCO3) dan topografi nano juga meningkatkan penetasan larva <cite id="f467f541-0">Larva karang menunjukkan preferensi penetasan yang dipengaruhi oleh sinyal mineral anorganik (misalnya SiO2 dan SrCO3) dan fitur topografis lokal skala puluhan nanometer, melebihi pengaruh rata-rata roughness dan ketegangan permukaan</cite> <cite id="f467f541-4">Diantara keramik alumina, CaCO3, dan beton sebagai permukaan tetes, beton menunjukkan penetasan larva tertinggi (1,92 ± 0,10 larva/cm²), tetapi kelangsungan hidup spata tertinggi terjadi pada CaCO3 (73,4 ± 4,2%); dominasi tumbuhnya koral lumut (Crustaphytum) dan alga coklat (Lobophora) menurunkan kelangsungan hidup</cite> <cite id="f467f541-1">Tanah liat terakota digunakan secara luas sebagai permukaan penetasan larva di lapangan untuk Pocillopora damicornis</cite>. 
- Untuk transplantasi karang dewasa, substrat buatan yang paling umum dan tahan lama adalah beton/batu bata (blok struktural) dan permukaan keras dengan penyangga hidrolik stabil; alternatif termasuk rebar, botol kaca daur ulang, keramik/epoksi yang dipelapis anti-karat, serta substrat 3D cetak/ biopolimer yang meningkatkan adhesi jaringan; keberhasilan utama bergantung pada orientasi fragmen, penambatan kuat, dan pengurangan stres mekanis jangka pendek <cite id="2aef01d7-0">Blok beton digunakan untuk memstabilkan dasar dan mengikat fragmen karang; botol kaca dan rebar diuji sebagai substrat penambat, dan fragmen yang diberi tali nylon/kabel lebih cepat menempel dibanding kawat logam atau tali kapas</cite> <cite id="193bd483-0">Nursery di Kepulauan Lakshadweep menggunakan rangka besi dan kawat dipleks sebagai kerangka, dengan blok beton 25×20 cm sebagai substrat penambatan; lapisan epoxy tahan karat diterapkan untuk daya tahan lingkungan</cite> <cite id="193bd483-2">Substrat buatan untuk transplantasi meliputi struktur beton, keramik, kawat dipleks, dan lainnya; material harus tahan lama dan sesuai kondisi hidrodinamik ekstrem</cite> <cite id="2aef01d7-4">Transplantasi fragmen Acropora pada struktur blok beton multitier menunjukkan orientasi vertikal/horizontal dan kabel tie efektif; permukaan bawah struktur sering tertutup endapan, sehingga dihindari</cite> <cite id="193bd483-3">Penyangga kabel nylon meningkatkan laju penempelan dan mengurangi detasmen dibanding kawat dan tali kapas; setelah 90 hari detasmen adalah 3,8% untuk kabel vs 25,3% dan 69,3% untuk kawat/tali</cite> <cite id="193bd483-4">Fragmen melekat lebih baik pada botol kaca daripada rebar, meski rebar kurang cenderung lepas; kabel tie paling efektif secara keseluruhan</cite> <cite id="193bd483-1">Rubble terkait jaring/net dapat menjadi substrat alternatif rendah biaya yang stabil dan berpermukaan kompleks untuk transplantasi karang</cite> <cite id="2aef01d7-2">3D-printed hybrid nurseries menggabungkan substrat biomimetik (keramik besar) dan mesh interlocking untuk menampung banyak fragmen dan meningkatkan scaling</cite> <cite id="2aef01d7-3">Resin berbasis minyak kacang dan kalsium karbonat yang dicetak 3D mendukung adhesi dan proliferasi sel karang serta menunjukkan penetasan awal karang pada plug buatan</cite>.

Apa yang paling efektif untuk rekrutmen larva
- Jenis substrat: Beton, keramik CaCO3, dan terakota
  - Beton cenderung menarik lebih banyak larva karena permukaan kasar dan sinyal kimia, sementara keramik CaCO3 dan permukaan CaCO3 biasanya memberikan kelangsungan hidup spata lebih tinggi karena ketahanan terhadap kompetisi alga awal; terakota sering dipakai di lapangan sebagai permukaan tetes dan memiliki histori penggunaan jangka panjang <cite id="f467f541-4">Beton menunjukkan penetasan larva tertinggi tetapi CaCO3 menawarkan kelangsungan hidup spata tertinggi; kompetisi dengan koral lumut dan alga coklat dominan</cite> <cite id="f467f541-1">Penggunaan tiles terakota yang diangkat dari bangunan sebagai permukaan larval settlement untuk Pocillopora damicornis di Sri Lanka</cite>. 
  - Komposit anorganik dan mineral tambahan (pasir, kaca, garam alkali tanah, SiO2, SrCO3) meningkatkan preferensi penetasan; larva mampu mendeteksi fitur topografis skala <100 nm dan menanggapi mineral larut, sehingga substrat “berciri kimia” dan “berotot nano” efektif <cite id="f467f541-0">Larva mendeteksi fitur topografis lokal jauh lebih kecil dari ukuran tubuh dan merespons mineral seperti SiO2 dan SrCO3; substrat komposit CaCO3 dengan penambahan dapat dirancang meningkatkan penetasan dan pertumbuhan pasca-metamorfosis</cite>.
- Persyaratan praktis: 
  - Permukaan kasar/pori dan biofilm awal mendorong penetasan larva; namun, keberagaman epifon kompetitif (alga coklat, koral lumut) dan herbivora yang memilih permukaan keras juga meningkatkan kematian spata; sehingga pengelolaan hidrolik (alur aliran untuk mengurangi endapan), antifouling sementara, dan penekanan pertumbuhan alga menjadi kunci <cite id="f467f541-4">Pengaruh material dominan terhadap komposisi alga pada tile; peningkatan penetasan pada beton tetapi penurunan kelangsungan hidup akibat dominasi Crustaphytum dan Lobophora</cite> <cite id="f467f541-3">Struktur dengan permukaan miring atau mesh mencegah penumpukan sedimen dan digunakan untuk koloni di lingkungan sedimen tinggi; nursery memberikan habitat sementara dan meningkatkan pertumbuhan fragmen</cite>.
- Rekomendasi umum: 
  - Untuk penangkaran/penetapan jangka pendek, gunakan permukaan CaCO3/keramik CaCO3 atau beton dengan perlakuan antifouling dan perawatan rutin pengendalian alga; tambahkan ciri mineral menarik (misalnya, pasir kuarsa/SiO2, atau senyawa strontium) dan struktur berpori/beralur mikro untuk menangkap biofilm bermanfaat <cite id="f467f541-0">Sinyal mineral dan topografi nano dapat dikombinasikan untuk meningkatkan penetasan dan pertumbuhan pasca-settling</cite> <cite id="f467f541-4">CaCO3 memberikan kelangsungan hidup spata tertinggi dibanding keramik alumina dan beton meskipun penetasan lebih rendah</cite>.
  - Untuk skala besar di laut terbuka, terakota dan beton tetap praktis; pastikan permukaan tidak tergenangi sedimen dan tutup area larva dengan kawat/tembok biologis sementara untuk mengurangi kompetitor <cite id="f467f541-1">Tiles terakota di pasang sebagai permukaan tetes di lokasi bermacet untuk menghitung spats</cite> <cite id="f467f541-3">Struktur buatan di Singapura menggunakan permukaan miring dan mesh untuk mengatasi sedimen; tiles juga menarik rekrutmen alami</cite>.

Apa yang paling efektif untuk transplantasi karang dewasa
- Jenis substrat: Beton/struktur stabil; keramik/epoksi; rebar; botol kaca daur ulang; mesh interlocking; dan substrat cetak/ biopolimer
  - Struktur beton (blok, APR multi-tier) adalah pilihan umum karena bobot dan daya dukung hidrodinamik; permukaan disusun bertingkat dan orientasi fragmen diatur untuk meminimalkan erosi dan detasmen awal <cite id="2aef01d7-0">Blok beton diisi dengan botol/ rebar sebagai penyangga untuk mengikat fragmen karang di lokasi rehabilitasi</cite> <cite id="2aef01d7-4">APR multi-tier dari beton dengan tingkat 20 cm; fragmen ditempatkan di level atas/menengah; permukaan bawah sering sedimen sehingga dihindari</cite> <cite id="193bd483-0">Kerangka besi dengan blok beton dan lapis epoxy tahan karat digunakan untuk nursery</cite>.
  - Material alternatif termasuk rebar (tahan lama dan kuat secara mekanis) dan botol kaca (permukaan CaCO3 alami, upcycling di pulau-pulau berkarang) yang menunjukkan penambatan efektif; namun, catatan beberapa studi menunjukkan kelangsungan hidup spata pada keramik kaca bisa lebih rendah dibanding substrat lain, sehingga perlu optimasi penambatan dan perawatan <cite id="193bd483-2">Rebar dan keramik digunakan sebagai substrat buatan yang tahan lama, dengan rebar cocok di daerah cuaca ekstrem</cite> <cite id="193bd483-4">Fragmen menempel lebih baik pada botol kaca daripada rebar; sebagian studi melaporkan survivorship spata pada tile kaca lebih rendah dibanding material tertentu</cite> <cite id="2aef01d7-0">Kombinasi botol dan rebar dengan tali nylon/kawat menunjukkan penambatan yang efektif</cite>.
  - Substrat ringan/terjangkau: modifikasi rubble dikuncinya dengan jaring/nylon/PE dan lapisan net/kawat; memberikan kompleksitas permukaan dan stabilitas lokal yang memungkinkan transplantasi karang di daerah rusak dengan biaya rendah <cite id="193bd483-1">Rubble dikemas dalam jaring (nylon/PE) sebagai substrat alternatif rendah biaya yang stabil dan berpermukaan kompleks, sukses menggantikan beton dan didukung pertumbuhan karang</cite>.
  - Teknologi baru: 3D-printed scaffold dari resin ramah lingkungan CaCO3 dan mesh biomimetik/keramik hybrid meningkatkan adhesi jaringan, proliferasi sel, dan menunjukkan penetasan awal karang pada plug; cocok untuk nursery dan outplanting skala besar <cite id="2aef01d7-2">Hybrid nurseries dengan substrat biomimetik dan mesh interlocking meningkatkan out-planting dan kesehatan jaringan fragmen</cite> <cite id="2aef01d7-3">Resin berbasis minyak kacang dan CaCO3 yang dicetak 3D menunjukkan adhesi dan proliferasi sel karang serta penetasan awal pada plug buatan</cite> <cite id="2aef01d7-3">Eksperimen fragmentasi mikro menunjukkan penempelan karang awal pada plug cetak</cite>.
- Faktor kritis untuk keberhasilan transplantasi:
  - Penambatan kuat dan cepat self-attachment: kabel nylon ratchet unggul dibanding kawat logam dan tali kapas; detasmen jangka pendek yang rendah krusial untuk mencegah mortalitas awal <cite id="193bd483-3">Kabel nylon menurunkan detasmen dari 69% (tali) hingga 3,8% setelah 90 hari, sementara meningkatkan penambatan (73% vs 30–57%)</cite> <cite id="193bd483-4">Kabel tie paling efektif; fragmen melekat lebih cepat pada botol kaca dibanding rebar, meski rebar lebih stabil secara mekanis</cite>.
  - Orientasi dan hidrodinamik: fragmen diorientasikan agar aliran mengalir melewati bagian bawah dan sisi yang kurang terlindung; hindari permukaan yang tertutup sedimen dan area resuspensi; struktur bertingkat memungkinkan distribusi vertikal <cite id="2aef01d7-4">APR multi-tier memberikan level transplasi dengan orientasi vertikal/horizontal dan membatasi penempatan di level bawah karena penutupan sedimen</cite> <cite id="193bd483-2">Di daerah cuaca ekstrem, material dan desain harus tahan lama dan sesuai dengan kondisi aliran</cite>.
  - Stres mekanis jangka pendek: monsun/arus kuat meningkatkan detasmen fisik; pemasangan dengan alat bantu dan penambatan ganda/penancapan rebar memperkuat kestabilan <cite id="2aef01d7-0">Stabilisasi dasar dengan blok beton, penambatan fragmen pada botol/rebar, dan penguatan dengan besi reinforcement untuk bertahan musim monsun</cite>.
  - Lingkungan dukung: di daerah sedimen tinggi, permukaan miring/mesh dan nursery berfungsi sebagai filter hidraulik untuk mengurangi penumpukan partikel dan meningkatkan pertumbuhan pasca-transplantasi <cite id="f467f541-3">Permukaan miring dan mesh mencegah penumpukan sedimen; nursery meningkatkan pertumbuhan dan biodiversitas di lingkungan sedimen tinggi</cite>.

Mengapa persyaratan substrat untuk larva dan transplantasi dewasa bertentangan?
- Kimia dan topografi: larva merespons sinyal mineral anorganik (SiO2, SrCO3) dan fitur topografis nano/akroskopik yang meningkatkan penetasan; sedangkan fragmen dewasa memerlukan permukaan kimia netral/ramah jaringan, rendah lekat-epifon patogen, dan struktur kuat agar tidak pecah/lepas; permukaan kasar yang “larva-friendly” cenderung lebih “macroalga-friendly” <cite id="f467f541-0">Larva karang menanggapi sinyal mineral dan topografi nano dengan positif, meningkatkan penetasan</cite> <cite id="f467f541-4">Permukaan CaCO3 mengurangi kompetisi dan meningkatkan kelangsungan hidup dibanding beton meskipun penetasan lebih rendah</cite>.

Title: Composite Substrates Reveal Inorganic Material Cues for Coral Larval Settlement
Snippet: : The widespread loss of stony reef-building coral populations has been compounded by the low settlement and survival of coral juveniles. These work ﬂ ows often make use of natural biochemical settlement cues, which are presented to swimming larvae to induce settlement. This paper establishes the potential for inorganic cues to complement these known biochemical e ﬀ ects. Settlement substrates were fabricated from calcium carbonate, a material present naturally on reefs, and modi ﬁ ed with additives including sands, glasses, and alkaline earth carbonates. Experiments with larvae of two Caribbean coral species revealed additive-speci ﬁ c settlement preferences that were independent of bulk surface properties such as mean roughness and wettability. Instead, analyses of the substrates suggest that settling coral larvae can detect localized topographical features more than an order of magnitude smaller than their body width and can sense and positively respond to soluble inorganic minerals such as silica (SiO 2 ) and strontianite (SrCO 3 ). Title: Enhancing Marine Biodiversity in Singapore’s Urbanizing Coastal Environment
Snippet: The loss of more than half of coral reef habitats to land reclamation and the exposure of the remaining reefs to chronic sedimentation necessitate active restoration interventions. This will complement the observed natural colonization by corals on seawalls and other structures along modified shores [29], [30]. Reef restoration efforts employing techniques that overcome sedimentation challenges have been demonstrated to be viable [31], [32]. These range from the provision of sloping solid substrata [33] or horizontal mesh surfaces that prevent sediment accumulation [34]. 

In-situ coral nurseries (Fig. 2) have a significant role in reef restoration efforts in a sediment-challenged environment [35]. Studies on two scleractinian species, Pachyseris speciosa and Pocillopora acuta (previously damicornis) [36], indicated that fragments raised in nurseries for five months before being transplanted to the reef substrate, grew significantly faster by three to five times compared to those that were transplanted directly without a nursery phase [37]. The faster growth of transplants in nurseries augmented their size and continued to manifest after they were transplanted to the reef, enabling them to perform better than the directly transplanted fragments. 

The coral nurseries themselves also served as microhabitats to enhance biodiversity despite the sedimentation, attracting a large variety of species such as fishes [38] and reef-associated invertebrates [39]. These nurseries also provided opportunities for recruitment, settlement and development of reef fauna. They enhance ecosystem functioning in degraded or non-reefal sites while at the same time nurture coral fragments for transplantation [32]. 

The biodiversity of artificial substrates developed through natural colonization can be enhanced by active transplantation particularly in the intertidal zone. Fragments of five species of scleractinian corals, three species of soft corals and three species of sponges reared in ex-situ nurseries prior to transplantation exhibited variable survivorship and growth.

Snippet: Sexual propagation of corals is a promising strategy for coral restoration, but one of the main challenges is the high mortality of coral spat due to competitive interactions with macroalgae during the early life history stages. Title: Exploring New Frontiers in Coral Nurseries: Leveraging 3D Printing Technology to Benefit Coral Growth and Survival

Title: Developing a sustainable resin for 3D printing in coral restoration
Snippet: Coral reefs boast one of the planet’s most diversified ecosystems, serving as an essential source of food and revenue for millions of people while providing shelter to a wide variety of marine creatures. In this study, we exploited 3D printing technology based on vat polymerization to fabricate artificial coral plugs, expediting the reef restoration process while minimizing labor costs. We have developed a scalable model through the photoinitiated polymerization of an eco-friendly resin composed of modified soybean oil and calcium carbonate which has the potential to significantly enhance global restoration efforts. Material characterization demonstrated that the printed scaffold was highly cross-linked. Based on cytotoxicity analysis, the printed scaffold exhibited excellent cell adhesion and proliferation characteristics. Unfortunately, most artificial substrates are expensive and use land-based material such asconcrete/cement-bases. In order to develop a new low-cost artificial substrate that can replace concrete/cement-base as amedia for coral transplantation, modified coral rubble was tested in a pilot study in Seribu Island, Jakarta. Two different nets (nylon and polyethylene) were used to form rubble into a compact shape, stable and strong substrate. The stability of therubble and the complexity of the surface which is created by the net make this substrate suitable for coral transplantation.Additionally, from an economic perspective the nets are very cheap and locally available. In a number of experiments,modified coral rubble successfully replaced the concrete /cement-base as a media for coral transplantation. The coral transplants were growing over time. With this method, we can try to rehabilitate the degraded coral reef destroyed by tsunami or other factors with material that already is available at the site and with less money. However, this approach requires testing at additional sites and for longer periods, to determine the replicability of the results.Key words: cement base, coral, rubble, transplantation

Title: The Art of Sticking: Attaching Methods Affect Direct Transplantation Success
Snippet: Marine ecosystems such as coral reefs are experiencing a rapid decline in the Anthropocene (Hughes et al. 2017) due to human-induced disturbances and natural phenomena such as hurricanes or monsoon periods (Hoegh-Guldberg et al. 2007;Hughes et al. 2003). Different approaches, like those used to recover damaged forests, have been attempted to rehabilitate degraded coral reefs over the past few decades abbreviated as "DT") involves attaching coral fragments from a donor to a recipient reef, and these are either attached to artificial structures (Fadli et al. 2012;Williams et al. 2019) or directly transplanted to the substrate (Forrester et al. 2012;Ladd et al. 2019;Lohr et al. 2017). Artificial structures are commonly used to increase coral cover by being deployed in damaged areas with abundant unconsolidated substrate, such as rubble patches (Fadli 2009;Ceccarelli et al. 2020). These include bamboo structures (Ferse 2010), metal frames (Bowden-Kerby 2001;Mahmoud et al. 2019), cement blocks (Chen et al. 2018), ceramic tiles (Forsman et al. 2015), giant clam valves (Dizon et al. 2008;Guest et al. 2011) or PVC frames (Abdo and Hegazy 2015), among others. The use of concrete structures has emerged aiming at either combining substrate stabilization with the provision of habitat structure or providing structure only (Ceccarelli et al. 2020;Razak et al. 2022). When performing a DT approach, it is crucial to use durable materials since they will become a part of the reef (Bowden-Kerby 1997;Lindahl 2003;Dizon et al. 2008). In areas subjected to extreme weather events, it is particularly important to use materials adapted to these conditions. Moreover, applying DT practices on stable substrates can accelerate their self-attachment rates, thus increasing their survival rates (Bowden-Kerby 1997; Edwards and Clark 1999;Lindahl 2003;Dizon and Yap 2006).
</snippet>
<snippet id=193bd483-3>
Title: The Art of Sticking: Attaching Methods Affect Direct Transplantation Success
Snippet: The success of coral reef rehabilitation practices is highly variable among projects and depends, in many cases, on their survivorship. While most research studies have focused on the long-term survival and growth rates of transplanted corals, short-term coral detachment is one of the principal causes of mortality in rehabilitation practices. Nonetheless, it is possible to prevent this by increasing the speed of coral self-attachment. To address this issue, we tested the efficiency of three different fasteners in attaching loose coral fragments onto two artificial substrata by assessing coral self-attachment and detachment rates in a short-term period (90 days). We transplanted 515 coral fragments from 8 species onto two substrates (glass bottles and iron rebar) using three fasteners (nylon cable tie, metal wire, and hemp rope). Generalized Linear Mixed-effect Models showed that the type of fastener, substrate, and the interactions between them were the main determinants of coral self-attachment and detachment. After 90 days, corals attached with cable ties exhibited lower detachment rates (3.80%) than corals attached with metal wire (25.28%) or hemp rope (69.27%). A higher number of fragments secured with cable ties managed to self-attach (73.42%) and grow over the substrate, compared with those secured with metal wire and hemp rope (57.3% and 30.18%, respectively).
</snippet>
<snippet id=193bd483-4>
Title: The Art of Sticking: Attaching Methods Affect Direct Transplantation Success
Snippet: The present study tested the efficiency of three fasteners (cable tie, metal wire, and hemp rope) in attaching coral fragments onto two materials (glass bottle and iron rebar) during the first three months after transplantation. Our results showed that coral fragments self-attached better on glass than on rebar, despite the latter's hardiness, especially when attached to the neck of the bottles. Still, coral fragments attached to rebar were less likely to detach over time. The main advantage of glass bottles is that they are an attractive upcycling alternative, especially on islands with resorts, whereas rebar usually needs to be specifically ordered. Some authors have previously used glass as an attachment substrate showing a high transplantation success (Chen et al. 2018;Hein et al. 2020). Nevertheless, it has been observed a low coral fragment survivorship for transplants grown on glass tiles, compared to another type of substrate (Dubininkas 2017). Self-attachment and growth of coral fragments influence coral rehabilitation success (Dizon et al. 2008;Shafir et al. 2010;Forrester et al. 2011;Guest et al. 2011;Tagliafico et al. 2018). While most studies have only focused on one method to secure coral fragments, some researchers have performed comparison studies among different attachment methods, such as epoxy versus superglue (Borneman and Lowrie 2001;Dizon et al. 2008), or cable ties and Z-epoxy (Forrester et al. 2011). 

Throughout our study, fragments attached with nylon cable ties grew new tissue over the glass bottles and rebar significantly faster (attachment rates: 75% and 70.97%, respectively) than those secured with metal wire (70.18% and 34.38%, respectively) and hemp rope (19.83% and 49.21%, respectively). Our results suggest that nylon cable ties were the most effective fastener, partially due to their ratchet system. This system has multiple advantages, such as its durability and simplicity when manipulating underwater, with minimal maintenance. Also, the transplants secured with cable ties in glass bottles and rebar had similar detachment rates to fragments attached with metal wire to glass bottles.

Apa yang paling efektif untuk rekrutmen larva
- Jenis substrat: Beton, keramik CaCO3, dan terakota
  - Beton cenderung menarik lebih banyak larva karena permukaan kasar dan sinyal kimia, sementara keramik CaCO3 dan permukaan CaCO3 biasanya memberikan kelangsungan hidup spata lebih tinggi karena ketahanan terhadap kompetisi alga awal; terakota sering dipakai di lapangan sebagai permukaan tetes dan memiliki histori penggunaan jangka panjang <cite id="f467f541-4">Beton menunjukkan penetasan larva tertinggi tetapi CaCO3 menawarkan kelangsungan hidup spata tertinggi; kompetisi dengan koral lumut dan alga coklat dominan</cite> <cite id="f467f541-1">Penggunaan tiles terakota yang diangkat dari bangunan sebagai permukaan larval settlement untuk Pocillopora damicornis di Sri Lanka</cite>. 
  - Komposit anorganik dan mineral tambahan (pasir, kaca, garam alkali tanah, SiO2, SrCO3) meningkatkan preferensi penetasan; larva mampu mendeteksi fitur topografis skala <100 nm dan menanggapi mineral larut, sehingga substrat “berciri kimia” dan “berotot nano” efektif <cite id="f467f541-0">Larva mendeteksi fitur topografis lokal jauh lebih kecil dari ukuran tubuh dan merespons mineral seperti SiO2 dan SrCO3; substrat komposit CaCO3 dengan penambahan dapat dirancang meningkatkan penetasan dan pertumbuhan pasca-metamorfosis</cite>.
- Persyaratan praktis: 
  - Permukaan kasar/pori dan biofilm awal mendorong penetasan larva; namun, keberagaman epifon kompetitif (alga coklat, koral lumut) dan herbivora yang memilih permukaan keras juga meningkatkan kematian spata; sehingga pengelolaan hidrolik (alur aliran untuk mengurangi endapan), antifouling sementara, dan penekanan pertumbuhan alga menjadi kunci <cite id="f467f541-4">Pengaruh material dominan terhadap komposisi alga pada tile; peningkatan penetasan pada beton tetapi penurunan kelangsungan hidup akibat dominasi Crustaphytum dan Lobophora</cite> <cite id="f467f541-3">Struktur dengan permukaan miring atau mesh mencegah penumpukan sedimen dan digunakan untuk koloni di lingkungan sedimen tinggi; nursery memberikan habitat sementara dan meningkatkan pertumbuhan fragmen</cite>.
- Rekomendasi umum: 
  - Untuk penangkaran/penetapan jangka pendek, gunakan permukaan CaCO3/keramik CaCO3 atau beton dengan perlakuan antifouling dan perawatan rutin pengendalian alga; tambahkan ciri mineral menarik (misalnya, pasir kuarsa/SiO2, atau senyawa strontium) dan struktur berpori/beralur mikro untuk menangkap biofilm bermanfaat <cite id="f467f541-0">Sinyal mineral dan topografi nano dapat dikombinasikan untuk meningkatkan penetasan dan pertumbuhan pasca-settling</cite> <cite id="f467f541-4">CaCO3 memberikan kelangsungan hidup spata tertinggi dibanding keramik alumina dan beton meskipun penetasan lebih rendah</cite>.
  - Untuk skala besar di laut terbuka, terakota dan beton tetap praktis; pastikan permukaan tidak tergenangi sedimen dan tutup area larva dengan kawat/tembok biologis sementara untuk mengurangi kompetitor <cite id="f467f541-1">Tiles terakota di pasang sebagai permukaan tetes di lokasi bermacet untuk menghitung spats</cite> <cite id="f467f541-3">Struktur buatan di Singapura menggunakan permukaan miring dan mesh untuk mengatasi sedimen; tiles juga menarik rekrutmen alami</cite>.

Apa yang paling efektif untuk transplantasi karang dewasa
- Jenis substrat: Beton/struktur stabil; keramik/epoksi; rebar; botol kaca daur ulang; mesh interlocking; dan substrat cetak/ biopolimer
  - Struktur beton (blok, APR multi-tier) adalah pilihan umum karena bobot dan daya dukung hidrodinamik; permukaan disusun bertingkat dan orientasi fragmen diatur untuk meminimalkan erosi dan detasmen awal <cite id="2aef01d7-0">Blok beton diisi dengan botol/ rebar sebagai penyangga untuk mengikat fragmen karang di lokasi rehabilitasi</cite> <cite id="2aef01d7-4">APR multi-tier dari beton dengan tingkat 20 cm; fragmen ditempatkan di level atas/menengah; permukaan bawah sering sedimen sehingga dihindari</cite> <cite id="193bd483-0">Kerangka besi dengan blok beton dan lapis epoxy tahan karat digunakan untuk nursery</cite>.
  - Material alternatif termasuk rebar (tahan lama dan kuat secara mekanis) dan botol kaca (permukaan CaCO3 alami, upcycling di pulau-pulau berkarang) yang menunjukkan penambatan efektif; namun, catatan beberapa studi menunjukkan kelangsungan hidup spata pada keramik kaca bisa lebih rendah dibanding substrat lain, sehingga perlu optimasi penambatan dan perawatan <cite id="193bd483-2">Rebar dan keramik digunakan sebagai substrat buatan yang tahan lama, dengan rebar cocok di daerah cuaca ekstrem</cite> <cite id="193bd483-4">Fragmen menempel lebih baik pada botol kaca daripada rebar; sebagian studi melaporkan survivorship spata pada tile kaca lebih rendah dibanding material tertentu</cite> <cite id="2aef01d7-0">Kombinasi botol dan rebar dengan tali nylon/kawat menunjukkan penambatan yang efektif</cite>.
  - Substrat ringan/terjangkau: modifikasi rubble dikuncinya dengan jaring/nylon/PE dan lapisan net/kawat; memberikan kompleksitas permukaan dan stabilitas lokal yang memungkinkan transplantasi karang di daerah rusak dengan biaya rendah <cite id="193bd483-1">Rubble dikemas dalam jaring (nylon/PE) sebagai substrat alternatif rendah biaya yang stabil dan berpermukaan kompleks, sukses menggantikan beton dan didukung pertumbuhan karang</cite>.
  - Teknologi baru: 3D-printed scaffold dari resin ramah lingkungan CaCO3 dan mesh biomimetik/keramik hybrid meningkatkan adhesi jaringan, proliferasi sel, dan menunjukkan penetasan awal karang pada plug; cocok untuk nursery dan outplanting skala besar <cite id="2aef01d7-2">Hybrid nurseries dengan substrat biomimetik dan mesh interlocking meningkatkan out-planting dan kesehatan jaringan fragmen</cite> <cite id="2aef01d7-3">Resin berbasis minyak kacang dan CaCO3 yang dicetak 3D menunjukkan adhesi dan proliferasi sel karang serta penetasan awal pada plug buatan</cite> <cite id="2aef01d7-3">Eksperimen fragmentasi mikro menunjukkan penempelan karang awal pada plug cetak</cite>.
- Faktor kritis untuk keberhasilan transplantasi:
  - Penambatan kuat dan cepat self-attachment: kabel nylon ratchet unggul dibanding kawat logam dan tali kapas; detasmen jangka pendek yang rendah krusial untuk mencegah mortalitas awal <cite id="193bd483-3">Kabel nylon menurunkan detasmen dari 69% (tali) hingga 3,8% setelah 90 hari, sementara meningkatkan penambatan (73% vs 30–57%)</cite> <cite id="193bd483-4">Kabel tie paling efektif; fragmen melekat lebih cepat pada botol kaca dibanding rebar, meski rebar lebih stabil secara mekanis</cite>.
  - Orientasi dan hidrodinamik: fragmen diorientasikan agar aliran mengalir melewati bagian bawah dan sisi yang kurang terlindung; hindari permukaan yang tertutup sedimen dan area resuspensi; struktur bertingkat memungkinkan distribusi vertikal <cite id="2aef01d7-4">APR multi-tier memberikan level transplasi dengan orientasi vertikal/horizontal dan membatasi penempatan di level bawah karena penutupan sedimen</cite> <cite id="193bd483-2">Di daerah cuaca ekstrem, material dan desain harus tahan lama dan sesuai dengan kondisi aliran</cite>.
  - Stres mekanis jangka pendek: monsun/arus kuat meningkatkan detasmen fisik; pemasangan dengan alat bantu dan penambatan ganda/penancapan rebar memperkuat kestabilan <cite id="2aef01d7-0">Stabilisasi dasar dengan blok beton, penambatan fragmen pada botol/rebar, dan penguatan dengan besi reinforcement untuk bertahan musim monsun</cite>.
  - Lingkungan dukung: di daerah sedimen tinggi, permukaan miring/mesh dan nursery berfungsi sebagai filter hidraulik untuk mengurangi penumpukan partikel dan meningkatkan pertumbuhan pasca-transplantasi <cite id="f467f541-3">Permukaan miring dan mesh mencegah penumpukan sedimen; nursery meningkatkan pertumbuhan dan biodiversitas di lingkungan sedimen tinggi</cite>.

Mengapa persyaratan substrat untuk larva dan transplantasi dewasa bertentangan?
- Kimia dan topografi: larva merespons sinyal mineral anorganik (SiO2, SrCO3) dan fitur topografis nano/akroskopik yang meningkatkan penetasan; sedangkan fragmen dewasa memerlukan permukaan kimia netral/ramah jaringan, rendah lekat-epifon patogen, dan struktur kuat agar tidak pecah/lepas; permukaan kasar yang “larva-friendly” cenderung lebih “macroalga-friendly” <cite id="f467f541-0">Larva karang menanggapi sinyal mineral dan topografi nano dengan positif, meningkatkan penetasan</cite> <cite id="f467f541-4">Permukaan CaCO3 mengurangi kompetisi dan meningkatkan kelangsungan hidup dibanding beton meskipun penetasan lebih rendah</cite>.
- Bioperformansi awal: peningkatan penetasan larva pada beton/keramik kasar berbanding terbalik dengan kenaikan pertumbuhan/kehidupan spata akibat epifon kompetitif (koral lumut, alga coklat) dan herbivora yang mengonsumsi permukaan keras; untuk transplantasi, prioritasnya adalah daya tahan jangka pendek dan pertumbuhan, sehingga permukaan yang minim stres biologis dan mekanis lebih diinginkan <cite id="f467f541-4">Penetasan terbesar pada beton tetapi kelangsungan hidup tertinggi pada CaCO3; interaksi kompetitif kuat antara spata dengan Crustaphytum dan Lobophora</cite> <cite id="f467f541-3">Koloni alami pada substrat buatan menarik biodiversitas, tetapi di lingkungan sedimen tinggi perlu desain yang mencegah penumpukan dan meningkatkan keberhasilan transplantasi</cite>.
- Stuktur dan hidrodinamik: larva memerlukan porositas, aliran biofilm, dan permukaan berliku untuk penempelan; fragmen dewasa memerlukan permukaan relatif rata/terkubur sedikit dan struktur stabil untuk mengurangi detasmen akibat arus; oleh karena itu, substrat “larva-optimal” (kasar/berpori) sering kurang ideal untuk transplantasi di aliran tinggi jangka panjang <cite id="2aef01d7-4">Transplantasi di level bawah pada APR dihindari karena tertutup sedimen/resuspension; orientasi dan penambatan memengaruhi stabilitas</cite> <cite id="193bd483-2">Material dan desain substrat harus tahan lama dan sesuai hidrodinamik; di daerah ekstrem, kekuatan mekanis utama</cite>.
- Ekosistem dan manajemen: substrat yang menyerap sedimen dan tumbuh cepat oleh alga memberikan habitat yang baik untuk larva, tetapi juga meningkatkan kompetisi dan herbivori terhadap transplant; untuk restorasi fungsional, substrat dipilih untuk menyeimbangkan rekrutmen alami dengan pertumbuhan fragmen yang cepat dan kehilangan yang rendah, sering dengan penutup hidraulik sementara dan pengendalian alga <cite id="f467f541-4">Kompetisi alga pada permukaan beton menurunkan kelangsungan hidup</cite> <cite id="f467f541-3">Nursery dan struktur miring/mesh meningkatkan biodiversitas dan pertumbuhan; teknik ini diadaptasi di lingkungan sedimen tinggi</cite>.

Rekomendasi praktis berdasarkan tujuan
- Jika tujuannya rekrutmen larva (habitat penetasan dan penyerapan genetik):
  - Pilih beton/keramik/terakota dengan modifikasi permukaan nano/pori dan tambahkan mineral menarik (SiO2, SrCO3) pada komposit CaCO3; pastikan sirkulasi air yang tidak terlalu kuat untuk menjaga biofilm bermanfaat dan mengurangi erosi permukaan <cite id="f467f541-0">Larva merespons mineral dan topografi nano; komposit CaCO3 dengan additives dapat meningkatkan penetasan</cite> <cite id="f467f541-4">Beton menarik larva lebih banyak tetapi alga kompetitor dominan; CaCO3 meningkatkan kelangsungan hidup</cite> <cite id="f467f541-1">Tiles terakota efektif secara lapangan untuk penetasan larva</cite>.
- Jika tujuannya transplantasi dewasa (restorasi struktur populasi):
  - Fokus pada substrat keras yang stabil hidrodinamik: beton bertingkat/APR, keramik/epoksi tahan karat, rebar/besi dengan penyangga kabel nylon ratchet; hindari permukaan tergenang sedimen dan area resuspension; gunakan mesh interlocking/3D-printed hybrid untuk skala besar; evaluasi pertumbuhan dan detasmen 3–6 bulan awal <cite id="2aef01d7-4">APR multi-tier dan orientasi/penambatan yang tepat meningkatkan stabilitas transplant</cite> <cite id="193bd483-3">Kabel nylon mengurangi detasmen hingga 3,8% setelah 90 hari dan meningkatkan penambatan</cite> <cite id="2aef01d7-2">Mesh interlocking dan hybrid design meningkatkan out-planting dan kesehatan jaringan</cite> <cite id="193bd483-0">Blok beton + epoxy tahan karat digunakan di nursery</cite>.
- Integrasi strategi (hybrid):
  - Gunakan substrat CaCO3/keramik untuk larval settlement di celah struktur beton/APR; tutup permukaan terbuka dengan kawat dipleks/mesh biologis untuk menangkap larva sekaligus mengurangi kompetisi; terapkan antifouling sementara dan pembersihan parsial; di daerah sedimen tinggi, tambahkan permukaan miring/mesh untuk aliran <cite id="f467f541-4">Material memengaruhi komposisi alga pada tile; kombinasi permukaan dan manajemen dapat menyeimbangkan penetasan dan kelangsungan hidup</cite> <cite id="f467f541-3">Struktur miring/mesh dan nursery meningkatkan kolonisasi alami dan pertumbuhan fragmen di lingkungan sedimen tinggi</cite>.

Catatan regional dan konteks Indonesia
- Di Indonesia dan kawasan Samudra Hindia, penggunaan terakota/beton, kawat dipleks, dan teknik “transplantasi langsung” di lokasi rusak sudah umum; penguasaan teknik penambatan (kabel tie, epoxy, rebar) dan pemilihan substrat sesuai energi arus monsun krusial <cite id="2aef01d7-0">Proyek di Singapura dan contoh pemasangan di Hindia Selatan menunjukkan praktik dengan beton, botol/rebar, dan kabel tie untuk menahan monsun</cite> <cite id="193bd483-2">Rebar dan keramik/epoxy sering dipilih di daerah cuaca ekstrem; material harus tahan lama</cite>.

Keterbatasan dan kebutuhan riset

Title: Composite Substrates Reveal Inorganic Material Cues for Coral Larval Settlement
Snippet: : The widespread loss of stony reef-building coral populations has been compounded by the low settlement and survival of coral juveniles. To rebuild coral communities, restoration practitioners have developed work ﬂ ows to settle vulnerable coral larvae in the laboratory and outplant settled juveniles back to natural and arti ﬁ cial reefs. These work ﬂ ows often make use of natural biochemical settlement cues, which are presented to swimming larvae to induce settlement. This paper establishes the potential for inorganic cues to complement these known biochemical e ﬀ ects. Settlement substrates were fabricated from calcium carbonate, a material present naturally on reefs, and modi ﬁ ed with additives including sands, glasses, and alkaline earth carbonates. Experiments with larvae of two Caribbean coral species revealed additive-speci ﬁ c settlement preferences that were independent of bulk surface properties such as mean roughness and wettability. Instead, analyses of the substrates suggest that settling coral larvae can detect localized topographical features more than an order of magnitude smaller than their body width and can sense and positively respond to soluble inorganic minerals such as silica (SiO 2 ) and strontianite (SrCO 3 ). These ﬁ ndings open a new area of research in coral reef restoration, in which composite substrates can be designed with a combination of natural organic and inorganic additives to increase larval settlement and perhaps also improve post-settlement growth, mineralization, and defense. of the lime mortar fabrication process and the fabrication of additional substrate types are provided in the Supporting Information along with details on substrate characterization methods. Larval Settlement Experiments. Test substrates with di ﬀ erent compositions were placed together in replicate 1 L polystyrene bins, each containing 800 mL of ﬁ ltered seawater (FSW), to evaluate larval settlement choices. FSW was prepared using a succession of stacked sediment ﬁ lters with pore sizes of 50, 20, 5, and 0.5 μ m (H 2 O Distributors, Marietta, GA). Settlement experiments were initiated by pipetting 200 larvae ( ± 5%) into each bin and ended after 7 days by recording settlement locations on the top and bottom of each substrate. Data were evaluated by one-way ANOVA with post hoc Tukey testing to determine signi ﬁ cance di ﬀ erences; more detailed statistical methods are provided in the Supporting

Title: Enhancing coral larval supply and seedling production using a special bundle collection system “coral larval cradle” for large‐scale coral restoration
Snippet: Although a huge pool (100-1,000 m 2 ) could hold all gametes from those mature corals, such a huge structure on the seabed would be easily broken by wind and waves, or too costly to make it durable. Consequently, the "larval cradle" was developed at a manageable size that can be constructed by a small group (i.e. two or three persons). Such cradles can be moved to target areas for restoration, and coral larvae can be easily released from a cradle. 

Our other aim was seedling production using an artificial settlement substrate within the cradle. It is well known that the initial mortality of Acropora settlers is very high, especially during the first 6 months after settlement (Wilson & Harrison 2005;Penin et al. 2011;Suzuki et al. 12018a, 12018b). We considered that appropriate settlement substrates could enhance post-settlement survival of coral settlers. In this study, therefore, we also devised a new settlement substratum for outplanting and then tested methods for optimizing larval settlement within a larval cradle. 

By integrating all of the elements mentioned above, we aimed to complete a sequential operating system for the mass production of coral larvae and seedlings in situ, and to upscale coral restoration under various situations.

Title: Enhancing Marine Biodiversity in Singapore’s Urbanizing Coastal Environment
Snippet: The loss of more than half of coral reef habitats to land reclamation and the exposure of the remaining reefs to chronic sedimentation necessitate active restoration interventions. This will complement the observed natural colonization by corals on seawalls and other structures along modified shores [29], [30]. Reef restoration efforts employing techniques that overcome sedimentation challenges have been demonstrated to be viable [31], [32]. These range from the provision of sloping solid substrata [33] or horizontal mesh surfaces that prevent sediment accumulation [34]. 

In-situ coral nurseries (Fig. 2) have a significant role in reef restoration efforts in a sediment-challenged environment [35]. Studies on two scleractinian species, Pachyseris speciosa and Pocillopora acuta (previously damicornis) [36], indicated that fragments raised in nurseries for five months before being transplanted to the reef substrate, grew significantly faster by three to five times compared to those that were transplanted directly without a nursery phase [37]. The faster growth of transplants in nurseries augmented their size and continued to manifest after they were transplanted to the reef, enabling them to perform better than the directly transplanted fragments. 

The coral nurseries themselves also served as microhabitats to enhance biodiversity despite the sedimentation, attracting a large variety of species such as fishes [38] and reef-associated invertebrates [39]. These nurseries also provided opportunities for recruitment, settlement and development of reef fauna. They enhance ecosystem functioning in degraded or non-reefal sites while at the same time nurture coral fragments for transplantation [32]. 

The biodiversity of artificial substrates developed through natural colonization can be enhanced by active transplantation particularly in the intertidal zone. Natural colonization shows the viability of hard structures such as seawalls as habitats for biological communities [40] and transplantation can further enhance the structure's ecological value. Fragments of five species of scleractinian corals, three species of soft corals and three species of sponges reared in ex-situ nurseries prior to transplantation exhibited variable survivorship and growth.

Title: Effects of material type and surface roughness of settlement tiles on macroalgal colonisation and early coral recruitment success
Snippet: Sexual propagation of corals is a promising strategy for coral restoration, but one of the main challenges is the high mortality of coral spat due to competitive interactions with macroalgae during the early life history stages. Optimising the properties of settlement substrates such as material types and surface roughness has the potential to improve the survival of spat by limiting the recruitment and growth of macroalgae. In this study, we assessed the effects of modifying surface roughness across three different tile materials (alumina-based ceramic, calcium carbonate (CaCO3), and concrete) on the settlement success and post-settlement survivorship of Acropora kenti coral larvae in six mesocosm tanks, each with different established macroalgal communities. The macroalgal community compositions on the tiles were significantly different among material types, but not surface roughness, although the type and abundance of macroalgal species were heavily influenced by the established tank communities. Increasing surface roughness did not affect larval settlement success or spat survivorship. Substantially higher larval settlement density was found on concrete tiles (1.92 ± 0.10 larvae cm−2), but spat survival was the highest on CaCO3 tiles (73.4 ± 4.2% survived). Very strong competitive interactions were observed between spat and macroalgae, with overgrowth by the crustose coralline alga Crustaphytum sp. and the brown alga Lobophora sp. being the primary cause of spat mortality. Overall, when taking into account both settlement and survival rates, concrete was the best performing among the tile types tested here.

Title: The Art of Sticking: Attaching Methods Affect Direct Transplantation Success
Snippet: We placed the collected fragments in a 20 L bucket with saltwater for their transportation by boat to the rehabilitation areas. Before being transplanted, we allocated these fragments on a rubble patch close to the rehabilitation site for 24 h to reduce possible stress produced during the collection (Forrester et al. 2012). 

We delimited three damaged reef areas of 10 m 2 each at Middle Reef for rehabilitation purposes. We stabilized the seafloor by placing twenty-four concrete structures of approximately 50 × 30 × 20 cm in size and about 30 kg. in weight each. Concrete structures have been used in reef rehabilitation for stabilizing regions or unconsolidated substrates since they are heavy and durable (Ceccarelli et al. 2020). We made each block by pouring concrete into a wooden frame with 6 to 8 glass bottles, where we attached the coral fragments. We transported the blocks by boat and sunk them in the sandy region nearby the rehabilitation areas, using SCUBA diving equipment and lifting bags to move them to their final location. To ensure that the structures would remain in place during the monsoon period, we secured the blocks to the rubble substrates with steel reinforcement bars (hereafter called rebar). 

To assess the suitability of different artificial substrates, we compared a common material used worldwide (rebar) and a novel material with great potential (glass bottles). We inserted eight glass bottles or eight pieces of rebar on each block, and we attached one coral transplant on each glass Coral fragments were collected from Riverview House-Reef and Middle Reef for transplantation in the study site at Middle Reef low availability, and the results were unsuccessful, labor intensive and time consuming. Marine epoxy might be more suitable in low or moderate-energy environments. We outplanted 158 fragments with nylon cable ties (96 to glass bottles and 62 to rebar), 178 with galvanized metal wire (114 coral fragments to glass bottles and 64 to rebar), and 179 coral fragments with two pieces of hemp rope per fragment (116 to glass bottles and 63 to rebar). bottle (Fig. 2A) or rebar (Fig. 2B). We used three fasteners to attach coral fragments: nylon cable ties, a thin galvanized metal wire, and biodegradable hemp rope.

Title: Mechanistic study on the role of 3D-Printed biomimetic coral bone scaffolds in bone defect repair
Snippet: Moderate biomechanical stimuli help regulate cell activities and promote bone regeneration. By optimizing biocompatibility and biomechanical performance, 3D-printed biomimetic coral bone scaffolds can effectively play a significant role in bone defect repair, promoting the regeneration and healing of bone tissues. This comprehensive mechanism positions the scaffold as an innovative treatment method that holds promise to replace traditional bone transplantation methods [12].

Title: Exploring New Frontiers in Coral Nurseries: Leveraging 3D Printing Technology to Benefit Coral Growth and Survival
Snippet: Coral nurseries and associated techniques are the most common and widespread reef restoration methods worldwide. Due to the rapid decline of coral reefs, coral nurseries need to be eco-friendlier and adapted for effective upscaling to support large restoration projects. We suggest new design and fabrication processes associated with coral gardening and transplantation with 3D printing technology to offer a beneficial solution for growing coral fragments in on-land and underwater nurseries. We describe multiple combinations of building nurseries through the integration of biomimetic substrates and novel solutions for attaching coral fragments. Our methods are supported with supplemental testing of two hybrid substrate designs and coral mounting structures, building upon previous studies in the Gulf of Eilat/Aqaba (GoE/A), Red Sea. We identified and quantified marine invertebrates colonizing the surfaces of our substrates with environmental DNA (eDNA) by targeting the mitochondrial COI gene. We evaluated our coral fragments with and without our mounting structures to obtain an indication of total protein as a proxy for tissue health. We demonstrate the ability to design hybrid nurseries with custom mounting structures using biomimetic substrates, such as large ceramic artificial reefs, or with an interlocking mesh for holding numerous fragments to maximize out-planting efforts. We propose several methods for both land and underwater nurseries catered to various restoration initiatives for cost-effective up-scaling to meet the demands of global reef restoration.

Title: Developing a sustainable resin for 3D printing in coral restoration
Snippet: Coral reefs boast one of the planet’s most diversified ecosystems, serving as an essential source of food and revenue for millions of people while providing shelter to a wide variety of marine creatures. However, overfishing, pollution, climate change, and other factors collectively pose an escalating danger to coral reefs. Therefore, coral reef restoration efforts are urgently needed to save corals. In this study, we exploited 3D printing technology based on vat polymerization to fabricate artificial coral plugs, expediting the reef restoration process while minimizing labor costs. We have developed a scalable model through the photoinitiated polymerization of an eco-friendly resin composed of modified soybean oil and calcium carbonate which has the potential to significantly enhance global restoration efforts. Material characterization demonstrated that the printed scaffold was highly cross-linked. Based on cytotoxicity analysis, the printed scaffold exhibited excellent cell adhesion and proliferation characteristics. The coral microfragmentation experiment showed initial signs of coral settlement on the printed coral plugs. This work demonstrates that plant-based material and vat-polymerization-based 3D printing techniques hold promise for coral restoration.

snippet.text: Coral nurseries and associated techniques are the most common and widespread reef restoration methods worldwide. Due to the rapid decline of coral reefs, coral nurseries need to be eco-friendlier and adapted for effective upscaling to support large restoration projects. We suggest new design and fabrication processes associated with coral gardening and transplantation with 3D printing technology to offer a beneficial solution for growing coral fragments in on-land and underwater nurseries. We describe multiple combinations of building nurseries through the integration of biomimetic substrates and novel solutions for attaching coral fragments. Our methods are supported with supplemental testing of two hybrid substrate designs and coral mounting structures, building upon previous studies in the Gulf of Eilat/Aqaba (GoE/A), Red Sea. We identified and quantified marine invertebrates colonizing the surfaces of our substrates with environmental DNA (eDNA) by targeting the mitochondrial COI gene. We evaluated our coral fragments with and without our mounting structures to obtain an indication of total protein as a proxy for tissue health. We demonstrate the ability to design hybrid nurseries with custom mounting structures using biomimetic substrates, such as large ceramic artificial reefs, or with an interlocking mesh for holding numerous fragments to maximize out-planting efforts. We propose several methods for both land and underwater nurseries catered to various restoration initiatives for cost-effective up-scaling to meet the demands of global reef restoration.

snippet.text: Coral reefs boast one of the planet’s most diversified ecosystems, serving as an essential source of food and revenue for millions of people while providing shelter to a wide variety of marine creatures. However, overfishing, pollution, climate change, and other factors collectively pose an escalating danger to coral reefs. Therefore, coral reef restoration efforts are urgently needed to save corals. In this study, we exploited 3D printing technology based on vat polymerization to fabricate artificial coral plugs, expediting the reef restoration process while minimizing labor costs. We have developed a scalable model through the photoinitiated polymerization of an eco-friendly resin composed of modified soybean oil and calcium carbonate which has the potential to significantly enhance global restoration efforts. Material characterization demonstrated that the printed scaffold was highly cross-linked. Based on cytotoxicity analysis, the printed scaffold exhibited excellent cell adhesion and proliferation characteristics. The coral microfragmentation experiment showed initial signs of coral settlement on the printed coral plugs. This work demonstrates that plant-based material and vat-polymerization-based 3D printing techniques hold promise for coral restoration.

Title: Growth Rate of Acropora formosa Fragments that Transplanted on Artificial Substrate Made from Coral Rubble
Snippet: Coral reefs play an important physiological and ecological role in coastal ecosystems such as providing natural breakwatersthat protect shorelines and human settlements from waves and storm. Corals killed by tsunami, waves and storms are often degraded into rubble. This rubble is dynamic, easily shifted by currents and storms, which effectively forms â€˜â€˜killing fieldsâ€™â€™ forcoral juveniles, hindering coral recovery. In order to rehabilitate coral reefs, artificial substrates are used both for coral transplantation and recruitment. Unfortunately, most artificial substrates are expensive and use land-based material such asconcrete/cement-bases. In order to develop a new low-cost artificial substrate that can replace concrete/cement-base as amedia for coral transplantation, modified coral rubble was tested in a pilot study in Seribu Island, Jakarta. Two different nets (nylon and polyethylene) were used to form rubble into a compact shape, stable and strong substrate. The stability of therubble and the complexity of the surface which is created by the net make this substrate suitable for coral transplantation.Additionally, from an economic perspective the nets are very cheap and locally available. In a number of experiments,modified coral rubble successfully replaced the concrete /cement-base as a media for coral transplantation. The coral transplants were growing over time. With this method, we can try to rehabilitate the degraded coral reef destroyed by tsunami or other factors with material that already is available at the site and with less money. However, this approach requires testing at additional sites and for longer periods, to determine the replicability of the results.Key words: cement base, coral, rubble, transplantation

Title: The Art of Sticking: Attaching Methods Affect Direct Transplantation Success
Snippet: Marine ecosystems such as coral reefs are experiencing a rapid decline in the Anthropocene (Hughes et al. 2017) due to human-induced disturbances and natural phenomena such as hurricanes or monsoon periods (Hoegh-Guldberg et al. 2007;Hughes et al. 2003). Different approaches, like those used to recover damaged forests, have been attempted to rehabilitate degraded coral reefs over the past few decades abbreviated as "DT") involves attaching coral fragments from a donor to a recipient reef, and these are either attached to artificial structures (Fadli et al. 2012;Williams et al. 2019) or directly transplanted to the substrate (Forrester et al. 2012;Ladd et al. 2019;Lohr et al. 2017). Artificial structures are commonly used to increase coral cover by being deployed in damaged areas with abundant unconsolidated substrate, such as rubble patches (Fadli 2009;Ceccarelli et al. 2020). These include bamboo structures (Ferse 2010), metal frames (Bowden-Kerby 2001;Mahmoud et al. 2019), cement blocks (Chen et al. 2018), ceramic tiles (Forsman et al. 2015), giant clam valves (Dizon et al. 2008;Guest et al. 2011) or PVC frames (Abdo and Hegazy 2015), among others. The use of concrete structures has emerged aiming at either combining substrate stabilization with the provision of habitat structure or providing structure only (Ceccarelli et al. 2020;Razak et al. 2022). When performing a DT approach, it is crucial to use durable materials since they will become a part of the reef (Bowden-Kerby 1997;Lindahl 2003;Dizon et al. 2008). In areas subjected to extreme weather events, it is particularly important to use materials adapted to these conditions. Moreover, applying DT practices on stable substrates can accelerate their self-attachment rates, thus increasing their survival rates (Bowden-Kerby 1997; Edwards and Clark 1999;Lindahl 2003;Dizon and Yap 2006).

Title: The Art of Sticking: Attaching Methods Affect Direct Transplantation Success
Snippet: The success of coral reef rehabilitation practices is highly variable among projects and depends, in many cases, on their survivorship. While most research studies have focused on the long-term survival and growth rates of transplanted corals, short-term coral detachment is one of the principal causes of mortality in rehabilitation practices. Nonetheless, it is possible to prevent this by increasing the speed of coral self-attachment. To address this issue, we tested the efficiency of three different fasteners in attaching loose coral fragments onto two artificial substrata by assessing coral self-attachment and detachment rates in a short-term period (90 days). We transplanted 515 coral fragments from 8 species onto two substrates (glass bottles and iron rebar) using three fasteners (nylon cable tie, metal wire, and hemp rope). Generalized Linear Mixed-effect Models showed that the type of fastener, substrate, and the interactions between them were the main determinants of coral self-attachment and detachment. After 90 days, corals attached with cable ties exhibited lower detachment rates (3.80%) than corals attached with metal wire (25.28%) or hemp rope (69.27%). A higher number of fragments secured with cable ties managed to self-attach (73.42%) and grow over the substrate, compared with those secured with metal wire and hemp rope (57.3% and 30.18%, respectively).

Title: The Art of Sticking: Attaching Methods Affect Direct Transplantation Success
Snippet: The present study tested the efficiency of three fasteners (cable tie, metal wire, and hemp rope) in attaching coral fragments onto two materials (glass bottle and iron rebar) during the first three months after transplantation. Our results showed that coral fragments self-attached better on glass than on rebar, despite the latter's hardiness, especially when attached to the neck of the bottles. Still, coral fragments attached to rebar were less likely to detach over time. The main advantage of glass bottles is that they are an attractive upcycling alternative, especially on islands with resorts, whereas rebar usually needs to be specifically ordered. Some authors have previously used glass as an attachment substrate showing a high transplantation success (Chen et al. 2018;Hein et al. 2020). Nevertheless, it has been observed a low coral fragment survivorship for transplants grown on glass tiles, compared to another type of substrate (Dubininkas 2017). Self-attachment and growth of coral fragments influence coral rehabilitation success (Dizon et al. 2008;Shafir et al. 2010;Forrester et al. 2011;Guest et al. 2011;Tagliafico et al. 2018). While most studies have only focused on one method to secure coral fragments, some researchers have performed comparison studies among different attachment methods, such as epoxy versus superglue (Borneman and Lowrie 2001;Dizon et al. 2008), or cable ties and Z-epoxy (Forrester et al. 2011). 

Throughout our study, fragments attached with nylon cable ties grew new tissue over the glass bottles and rebar significantly faster (attachment rates: 75% and 70.97%, respectively) than those secured with metal wire (70.18% and 34.38%, respectively) and hemp rope (19.83% and 49.21%, respectively). Our results suggest that nylon cable ties were the most effective fastener, partially due to their ratchet system. This system has multiple advantages, such as its durability and simplicity when manipulating underwater, with minimal maintenance. Also, the transplants secured with cable ties in glass bottles and rebar had similar detachment rates to fragments attached with metal wire to glass bottles.

snippet.text:
The present study tested the efficiency of three fasteners (cable tie, metal wire, and hemp rope) in attaching coral fragments onto two materials (glass bottle and iron rebar) during the first three months after transplantation. Our results showed that coral fragments self-attached better on glass than on rebar, despite the latter's hardiness, especially when attached to the neck of the bottles. Still, coral fragments attached to rebar were less likely to detach over time. The main advantage of glass bottles is that they are an attractive upcycling alternative, especially on islands with resorts, whereas rebar usually needs to be specifically ordered. Some authors have previously used glass as an attachment substrate showing a high transplantation success (Chen et al. 2018;Hein et al. 2020). Nevertheless, it has been observed a low coral fragment survivorship for transplants grown on glass tiles, compared to another type of substrate (Dubininkas 2017). Self-attachment and growth of coral fragments influence coral rehabilitation success (Dizon et al. 2008;Shafir et al. 2010;Forrester et al. 2011;Guest et al. 2011;Tagliafico et al. 2018). While most studies have only focused on one method to secure coral fragments, some researchers have performed comparison studies among different attachment methods, such as epoxy versus superglue (Borneman and Lowrie 2001;Dizon et al. 2008), or cable ties and Z-epoxy (Forrester et al. 2011). 

Throughout our study, fragments attached with nylon cable ties grew new tissue over the glass bottles and rebar significantly faster (attachment rates: 75% and 70.97%, respectively) than those secured with metal wire (70.18% and 34.38%, respectively) and hemp rope (19.83% and 49.21%, respectively). Our results suggest that nylon cable ties were the most effective fastener, partially due to their ratchet system. This system has multiple advantages, such as its durability and simplicity when manipulating underwater, with minimal maintenance. Also, the transplants secured with cable ties in glass bottles and rebar had similar detachment rates to fragments attached with metal wire to glass bottles.

documents.title: Growth Rate of Acropora formosa Fragments that Transplanted on Artificial Substrate Made from Coral Rubble
documents.snippet: Coral reefs play an important physiological and ecological role in coastal ecosystems such as providing natural breakwatersthat protect shorelines and human settlements from waves and storm. Corals killed by tsunami, waves and storms are often degraded into rubble. This rubble is dynamic, easily shifted by currents and storms, which effectively forms â€˜â€˜killing fieldsâ€™â€™ forcoral juveniles, hindering coral recovery. In order to rehabilitate coral reefs, artificial substrates are used both for coral transplantation and recruitment. Unfortunately, most artificial substrates are expensive and use land-based material such asconcrete/cement-bases. In order to develop a new low-cost artificial substrate that can replace concrete/cement-base as amedia for coral transplantation, modified coral rubble was tested in a pilot study in Seribu Island, Jakarta. Two different nets (nylon and polyethylene) were used to form rubble into a compact shape, stable and strong substrate. The stability of therubble and the complexity of the surface which is created by the net make this substrate suitable for coral transplantation.Additionally, from an economic perspective the nets are very cheap and locally available. In a number of experiments,modified coral rubble successfully replaced the concrete /cement-base as a media for coral transplantation. The coral transplants were growing over time. With this method, we can try to rehabilitate the degraded coral reef destroyed by tsunami or other factors with material that already is available at the site and with less money. However, this approach requires testing at additional sites and for longer periods, to determine the replicability of the results.Key words: cement base, coral, rubble, transplantation

documents.snippet: Marine ecosystems such as coral reefs are experiencing a rapid decline in the Anthropocene (Hughes et al. 2017) due to human-induced disturbances and natural phenomena such as hurricanes or monsoon periods (Hoegh-Guldberg et al. 2007;Hughes et al. 2003). Different approaches, like those used to recover damaged forests, have been attempted to rehabilitate degraded coral reefs over the past few decades abbreviated as "DT") involves attaching coral fragments from a donor to a recipient reef, and these are either attached to artificial structures (Fadli et al. 2012;Williams et al. 2019) or directly transplanted to the substrate (Forrester et al. 2012;Ladd et al. 2019;Lohr et al. 2017). Artificial structures are commonly used to increase coral cover by being deployed in damaged areas with abundant unconsolidated substrate, such as rubble patches (Fadli 2009;Ceccarelli et al. 2020). These include bamboo structures (Ferse 2010), metal frames (Bowden-Kerby 2001;Mahmoud et al. 2019), cement blocks (Chen et al. 2018), ceramic tiles (Forsman et al. 2015), giant clam valves (Dizon et al. 2008;Guest et al. 2011) or PVC frames (Abdo and Hegazy 2015), among others. The use of concrete structures has emerged aiming at either combining substrate stabilization with the provision of habitat structure or providing structure only (Ceccarelli et al. 2020;Razak et al. 2022). When performing a DT approach, it is crucial to use durable materials since they will become a part of the reef (Bowden-Kerby 1997;Lindahl 2003;Dizon et al. 2008). In areas subjected to extreme weather events, it is particularly important to use materials adapted to these conditions. Moreover, applying DT practices on stable substrates can accelerate their self-attachment rates, thus increasing their survival rates (Bowden-Kerby 1997; Edwards and Clark 1999;Lindahl 2003;Dizon and Yap 2006).

documents.title: The Art of Sticking: Attaching Methods Affect Direct Transplantation Success
documents.snippet: The success of coral reef rehabilitation practices is highly variable among projects and depends, in many cases, on their survivorship. While most research studies have focused on the long-term survival and growth rates of transplanted corals, short-term coral detachment is one of the principal causes of mortality in rehabilitation practices. Nonetheless, it is possible to prevent this by increasing the speed of coral self-attachment. To address this issue, we tested the efficiency of three different fasteners in attaching loose coral fragments onto two artificial substrata by assessing coral self-attachment and detachment rates in a short-term period (90 days). We transplanted 515 coral fragments from 8 species onto two substrates (glass bottles and iron rebar) using three fasteners (nylon cable tie, metal wire, and hemp rope). Generalized Linear Mixed-effect Models showed that the type of fastener, substrate, and the interactions between them were the main determinants of coral self-attachment and detachment. After 90 days, corals attached with cable ties exhibited lower detachment rates (3.80%) than corals attached with metal wire (25.28%) or hemp rope (69.27%). A higher number of fragments secured with cable ties managed to self-attach (73.42%) and grow over the substrate, compared with those secured with metal wire and hemp rope (57.3% and 30.18%, respectively).
